question: Sannu. marori am woodi caɗeele — central shoot drying out — deadheart symptom. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: rice stem borer woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. moth larvae bore into stem. Ko mbaɗata: apply carbofuran granules at panicle initiation. Woto yejjito — fields near wild grasses have higher infestation.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for rice farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo fe mo bi mo se le sweet potato planting fun oko anamo mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori sweet potato planting fun anamo: plant healthy vines 25-30cm long. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe space 1m between rows, 30cm between plants. plant at start of rainy season.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta watermelon planting e ndemri kankana am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow watermelon planting e kankana: direct seed in field. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 2m between rows, 1m between plants. watermelon needs full sun and well-drained soil.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for watermelon farmers

question: Jam na. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta tea planting e ndemri shayi am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow tea planting e shayi: plant on well-drained slopes. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 1.5m between plants. prune regularly to encourage new growth.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for tea farmers

question: Eku oo, sweet potato mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate sweet potato with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Bawo ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le harvesting and storage fun oko ere mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori harvesting and storage fun ere: harvest when pods are dry. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe store in airtight PICS bags. protect from bruchid weevils in storage.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Ina fama da matsalar cashew ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Kedu. nduku m nwere nsogbu — holes in tubers with bitter taste. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: sweet potato weevil (Cylas puncticollis) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. weevil attacks underground. Ihe ị ga-eme: hill soil to cover exposed tubers. Echefula — rotate crops for 2 years.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Sannu. Na ga dark greasy spots on leaves and fruit rot a jikin tumatir ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: late blight (Phytophthora infestans) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus thrives in cool wet weather. Magani: spray mancozeb preventively. rotate tomatoes away from potato fields.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for tomato farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo ri wipe ila mi ni small round holes in leaves like shot pattern. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: okra flea beetle (Podagrica uniforma) lo n damu oko re. heavy infestation defoliates young plants. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: neem oil spray and ash dusting. Ma gbagbe — plant early to escape peak beetle season.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for okra farmers

question: E pele o. Mo ri wipe kofi mi ni small holes in coffee berries with damage inside. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni coffee berry borer (Hypothenemus hampei). most serious coffee pest globally. Ogba: harvest all ripe berries promptly. Mase gbagbe pe — use broca traps with ethanol-methanol mix.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for coffee farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. ayaba am woodi caɗeele — larvae tunnel into corm causing toppling. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: banana weevil (Cosmopolites sordidus) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. adults hide in crop residues. Ko mbaɗata: use clean planting material (tissue culture). Woto yejjito — trap adults with pseudostem discs.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for plantain farmers

question: Ina kwana. Ina so in san yadda zan onion planting a aikin albasa don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da onion planting a aikin albasa: direct seed or use nursery transplants. Wannan yana taimakawa domin space 20cm between rows, 10cm between plants. onions need full sun exposure.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for onion farmers

question: Kedu. akpu m nwere nsogbu — leaves appear bunched and distorted. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: cassava mealybug (Phenacoccus manihoti) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. mealybug sucks plant sap. Ihe ị ga-eme: release parasitic wasp Apoanagyrus lopezi for control. Echefula — significantly reduces tuber size.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for cassava farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Ahụrụ m dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit na ose m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: bacterial spot (Xanthomonas campestris) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na bacteria spread by rain splash. Ngwọta: copper spray at transplanting. use disease-free seed from reliable source.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for pepper farmers

question: E karo. Mo fe mo bi mo se le coffee maintenance fun oko kofi mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori coffee maintenance fun kofi: prune old branches. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe apply organic fertilizer annually. maintain good shade cover.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for coffee farmers

question: Kedu. Ahụrụ m purple-brown lesions on leaves that girdle them na yorobo m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: onion purple blotch (Alternaria porri) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus Alternaria porri. Ngwọta: spray mancozeb every 10 days. rotate away from allium fields for 3 years.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for onion farmers

question: Eku agba mi, rice mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Bronze-orange discolouration of older leaves ("bronzing") indicates iron toxicity, common in waterlogged, acidic soils. (1) Drain the field for 3-5 days to aerate the soil — this allows iron to precipitate out of the soil solution. (2) Apply lime (2-4 t/ha) to raise soil pH above 5.0. (3) Use NPK 15-15-15 fertiliser rather than single-nutrient fertilisers — potassium helps reduce iron uptake. (4) Plant tolerant varieties: NERICA-L series or TOX 4004. (5) In the next season, avoid continuous flooding of young seedlings; use alternate wetting and drying irrigation.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. koko m nwere nsogbu — feeding lesions on pods and shoots. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: cocoa mirids (Sahlbergella singularis) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. mirids inject toxic saliva. Ihe ị ga-eme: spray bifenthrin at recommended rates. Echefula — shade management reduces mirid population.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. Na ga water-soaked spots on leaves a jikin auduga ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: bacterial blight (Xanthomonas campestris pv. malvacearum) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar bacteria spread by rain. Magani: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for cotton farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le cashew planting fun oko kasu mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori cashew planting fun kasu: plant trees 10m apart. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe apply organic fertilizer. prune dead branches regularly.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for cashew farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta okra planting e ndemri la'ano am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow okra planting e la'ano: sow seeds 2-3cm deep. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 60cm between rows, 30cm between plants. okra needs full sun and well-drained soil.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for okra farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. masara ta na da matsala — holes in leaves with larvae inside whorl. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. moths lay eggs at night on maize — larvae feed inside. Abin da za ka yi: spray neem (azadirachtin) at early growth stage. Kada ka manta — pest spreads fast without control — act within 3 days.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for maize farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo ri white powdery coating on leaves lori ila mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: powdery mildew lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spreads in dry season. Itoju: spray sulfur fungicide. remove infected leaves.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for okra farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Ahụrụ m angular brown spots on leaves na agwa m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for beans farmers

question: E karo. Mo ri yellow leaves with V-shaped lesions lori kabeji mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: black rot (Xanthomonas campestris) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa bacteria spread by water. Itoju: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 3 years.

question: Ndewo. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi plantain planting n'ugbo ogidi m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka plantain planting na ogidi: use healthy suckers from reliable source. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na space 3m between plants. apply mulch to conserve moisture.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for plantain farmers

question: Ek'abo. Mo ri yellow and white streaked leaves lori jero mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: downy mildew (Sclerospora graminicola) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spread by wind and rain. Itoju: use resistant varieties. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for millet farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. dabino ta na da matsala — larvae tunnel into trunk weakening the tree. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: palm weevil (Rhynchophorus phoenicis) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. adults attracted to wounds on trunk. Abin da za ka yi: avoid wounding trunk during pruning. Kada ka manta — pheromone traps for monitoring.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for oil palm farmers

question: Kedu. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi cashew planting n'ugbo kashu m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?

question: Kedu. nkwu m nwere nsogbu — larvae tunnel into trunk weakening the tree. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?

question: Mbaaɗa. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta sorghum planting e ndemri mbayeeri am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow sorghum planting e mbayeeri: sow seeds 3-5cm deep. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 75cm between rows, 20cm between plants. sorghum tolerates drought better than maize.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Jam na. kasu am woodi caɗeele — dead branches and holes in bark. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?

question: E karo. Mo ri wipe ata mi ni fruits rot from inside with maggots. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: pepper fruit fly (Bactrocera latifrons) lo n damu oko re. fly punctures fruit to lay eggs. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: harvest regularly before pest builds up. Ma gbagbe — bag young fruits with paper.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for pepper farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. Mi yi'i yellow leaves with white underside e sunflower am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?

question: Sannu. Na ga blisters on leaves turning white a jikin shayi ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: blister blight (Exobasidium vexans) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus spreads in misty weather. Magani: spray copper fungicide. prune for good air circulation.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for tea farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi grazing rotation n'ugbo mmiri ara m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka grazing rotation na mmiri ara: rotate grazing areas every week. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na allow pasture to rest between grazing. this prevents overgrazing and reduces disease.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for dairy farmers

question: Kedu. green m nwere nsogbu — holes in stems and wilting leaves. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: amaranth stem borer na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. moth larvae bore into stems. Ihe ị ga-eme: spray neem oil. Echefula — remove infected plants.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for amaranth farmers

question: Eku oo, yam mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: The yellow-green leaf pattern you describe is Cassava Mosaic Disease caused by geminiviruses transmitted by whiteflies. There is no chemical cure. (1) Uproot and burn ALL affected plants immediately — do NOT use them as planting material. (2) Use certified mosaic-resistant varieties: TME 419, TMS 30572, or IITA-TMS-I011412. (3) Plant stakes at the recommended spacing of 1 m × 1 m. (4) Avoid recycling stakes from infected fields. (5) Intercrop with maize or cowpea to reduce whitefly populations. Contact your nearest IITA or NRCRI extension office for free resistant planting material.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar tea ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Translucent blisters on young leaves that turn brown and break indicate Blister Blight (Exobasidium vexans). (1) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L OR hexaconazole at 1 ml/L every 7-10 days during monsoon. (2) Maintain adequate shade (50-60%) — direct sunlight makes blister blight worse. (3) Pluck and destroy all affected leaves. (4) Apply balanced NPK (YTD or similar tea mixture) at recommended rates to maintain bush health. (5) Prune to maintain plucking table height — do NOT allow bushes to become too tall and dense. Pre-plucking interval: copper 7 days.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: No danyama. Mi yi'i yellow streaks on leaves e masar am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: Ɗo'o ko rafi wi'eteedo maize streak virus (MSV). O saakotoo e laawol leafhoppers. virus has no cure once established. Ko potɗaa waɗde: remove infected plants. virus has no cure once established.
source: NASC-Adamawa, disease diagnosis advisory for maize farmers

question: E ku ise o. Mo ri wipe owu mi ni larvae bore into bolls causing them to drop. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?

question: E karo. Mo ri wipe ifunni mi ni ticks on cattle body sucking blood. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: ticks (Rhipicephalus microplus) lo n damu oko re. ticks transmit diseases like East Coast fever. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: dip or spray cattle with acaricide every 2 weeks. Ma gbagbe — maintain clean grazing areas to reduce ticks.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for dairy farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. Mi yi'i dark spots on ripening fruit e mangoro am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo tomato m na-acha odo odo na ntụpọ ojii. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Dark, leathery rot at the blossom end of the fruit is blossom end rot — NOT a disease but a calcium disorder caused by irregular watering. (1) Water consistently — apply 25-30 mm of water per week, split across 2-3 sessions. Do NOT let the soil dry out then flood. (2) Apply gypsum (calcium sulfate) at 100 kg/ha before the next planting. (3) For immediate correction, spray calcium chloride (5 g/L) on the leaves and developing fruit every 5 days for 3 applications. (4) Mulch heavily (5 cm) to maintain even soil moisture. (5) Avoid excessive nitrogen fertiliser which causes rapid growth and calcium dilution. Remove affected fruit so the plant redirects energy to healthy ones.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo yam m nwere akara mosaic na akwukwo, osisi anaghi eto nke oma. Biko nyere m aka.

question: Eku agba mi, plantain mi ni awon aami bi mosaic lori ewe, ko si dagba daradara. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?

question: E ku aaro. Mo ri water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown lori ere mi. Arun wo ni eyi?

question: Sannu. Masara ta na da ramuka a cikin ganye, ina kuma ganin tsutsa a jikin ganye na sabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda), mafi hatsarin kwaro ga masara a Afirka. Kada ka damu da yawa — ana iya shawo kan ta ba tare da magunguna masu tsada ba. Abubuwan da za ka yi: (1) Idan gona karam ce, tara tsutsar da hannu a cikin mazubin masarar ka kuma ka kashe su. (2) A zuba man neem a cikin mazubin (a jiƙa ƙwayayen neem a ruwa dare daya, a tace sannan a fesa). (3) Idan gona babba ce, a yi amfani da maganin halitta kamar Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) — wannan maganin yana kashe tsutsa ne kawai, ba zai cutar da mutum ba. (4) A dasa masara da wuri, kuma a hada shi da wake-wake wanda ke rage yawan kwaro. (5) A guji amfani da magungunan kashe kwaro na roba kawai — juriya ya zama gama gari a Yammacin Afirka. Idan har yanzu kana da matsala, je ofishin noma na karamar hukumar ka.
source: FAO Fall Armyworm Control Guide, 2024; IITA Maize Program

question: Eku oo, coffee mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. (3) Apply carbofuran 3G granules at 0.75 kg a.i./ha into the whorl at knee-height stage. (4) After harvest, cut stubble to ground level and bury or burn crop residues to kill overwintering larvae. (5) Rotate with legumes (cowpea, groundnut) to break the pest cycle.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Assalamu alaikum. kiwo ta na da matsala — ticks on cattle body sucking blood. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: ticks (Rhipicephalus microplus) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. ticks transmit diseases like East Coast fever. Abin da za ka yi: dip or spray cattle with acaricide every 2 weeks. Kada ka manta — maintain clean grazing areas to reduce ticks.

question: Ina fama da matsalar pepper ta. Ganyayyakin sun ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near pepper to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. masar am woodi caɗeele — central leaves drying out (deadheart). Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?

question: Mo ni isoro pelu rice mi, awon ewe re ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Grey-whitish lesions on leaves with brown borders indicate rice blast (Magnaporthe grisea). This is the most destructive rice disease worldwide. (1) Avoid excessive nitrogen — limit urea to 60 kg/ha in blast-prone areas and split into 3 doses. (2) Spray tricyclazole at 0.6 g/L or isoprothiolane at 1 ml/L at first sign and repeat after 10-14 days. (3) Maintain 2-3 cm of standing water in the field; intermittent drying stresses plants and increases susceptibility. (4) Plant resistant varieties: NERICA 4, ARICA 3, or IR64. (5) Burn infected straw after harvest — the fungus survives in crop residue.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, onion mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini mo le se?
answer: Soft, rotting bulb base with white fungal growth indicates basal rot (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae). (1) Remove and destroy affected plants — do NOT store bulbs from infected rows. (2) Treat seed bulbs with Trichoderma viride (10 g/kg seed) before planting. (3) Avoid injury to bulbs during weeding. (4) Harvest when 50% of tops have fallen and cure bulbs in the sun for 7-10 days. (5) Store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place. (6) Rotate away from alliums for 4 years.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ewa mi ti gbẹ ati awọn ewe rẹ ti di ofeefee. Kini iṣoro?

question: Awon tomati mi ti baje ati pe awon eya ara re ti sun. Kini a le se?
answer: Awon tomati ti o baje ati ti o sun ni blossom-end rot. (1) Ko se aisan kokoro - o je aini kalisiomu (calcium). (2) Ma lo ajile nitrogen pupo - o da kalisiomu duro. (3) Rii pe ile ni kalisiomu to - fi awon epo eyin (egg shells) tabi lime kun ile. (4) Fi omi kun awon tomati ni deede - ma je ki ile gbe ju tabi tutu ju. (5) Lo mulch lati da omi duro. (6) Gbin awon tomati ti o le fa: Tengeru 97, Rio Grande. Kan si osise ADP.

question: Eku oo, yam mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. cowpea na suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Me zan yi?
answer: Stunted growth, yellowing, swollen root galls (knots), and wilting despite moist soil indicate root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). (1) There is no curative chemical treatment. (2) Incorporate fresh neem leaves or neem cake at 500 kg/ha into the soil 2 weeks before the next planting. (3) Solarize the soil with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks. (4) Plant marigold (Tagetes erecta) as a trap crop — its roots release natural nematicides. (5) Rotate with maize, sorghum, or millet for 2-3 seasons — these are non-hosts. (6) Apply well-composted manure at 5 t/ha; the microbial activity suppresses nematodes.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo groundnut m anaghị eto nke ọma, akwukwo na-akpọnwụ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Aflatoxin contamination is caused by Aspergillus fungi and is a serious food safety risk — it can cause liver disease. Prevention is everything: (1) Harvest at the right maturity — do NOT delay harvest, especially if rains are expected. (2) Dry produce rapidly and thoroughly to below 13% moisture. Use raised drying racks, not bare ground. (3) Store in hermetic (airtight) bags — PICS bags or metal silos — away from heat and moisture. (4) Sort and discard any grains that are discoloured, shriveled, or moldy BEFORE storage. (5) Apply Aflasafe (biocontrol product available in Nigeria, Kenya) at 10 kg/ha 2-3 weeks before flowering. (6) NEVER feed mouldy grain to livestock.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina kwana. shinkafa ta na da matsala — deadheart — central shoot wilts. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Ahụrụ m white powder on flowers and leaves na kashu m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

question: Sannu. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta rice planting e ndemri marori am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?

question: Barka dai. Na ga yellow leaves with V-shaped lesions a jikin kabeji ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: black rot (Xanthomonas campestris) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar bacteria spread by water. Magani: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 3 years.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Ina kwana. auduga ta na da matsala — larvae bore into bolls causing them to drop. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: cotton bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. polyphagous pest — also attacks tomato and maize. Abin da za ka yi: Bt cotton provides genetic resistance. Kada ka manta — spray neem kernel extract at flowering.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for cotton farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. Na ga pods turn black with white flour-like coating a jikin koko ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira black pod disease (Phytophthora megakarya). Yana yaduwa ta hanyar most serious cocoa disease in West Africa. harvest ripe pods promptly — delay increases rot. Abin yi: remove infected pods and spray copper fungicide. harvest ripe pods promptly — delay increases rot.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo tomato m nwere obere ahụhụ na akwụkwọ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Concentric ring spots on older leaves indicate early blight (Alternaria solani). (1) Remove affected lower leaves and burn them. (2) Spray chlorothalonil at 2 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 7-10 days. (3) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent soil splash. (4) Ensure adequate potassium — apply 100 kg/ha muriate of potash. (5) Rotate with non-solanaceous crops (maize, beans) for 2-3 years. (6) Stake plants to keep foliage off the ground. Pre-harvest interval: chlorothalonil 7 days.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Barka dai. Na ga brown spots on leaves and stems a jikin dawa ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: anthracnose (Colletotrichum graminicola) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus survives in crop residue. Magani: rotate crops for 2 years. spray fungicide at flowering.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri wipe tii mi ni dark spots on leaves and young shoots. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?

question: Assalamu alaikum. Na ga water-soaked spots on leaves and pods a jikin wake ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?

question: Barka da rana. Na ga discolored grains with fungal growth a jikin dawa ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira grain mold. Yana yaduwa ta hanyar high humidity at grain filling. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately. Abin yi: harvest at physiological maturity. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately.

question: Eku oo, mango mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini mo le se?
answer: Dark bore holes on fruit and larvae inside the seed indicate mango seed weevil (Sternochetus mangiferae). The adult lays eggs on developing fruit and larvae tunnel into the seed. (1) Collect and destroy ALL fallen fruit and seeds — the weevil completes its lifecycle in the seed. (2) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L when fruit are marble-sized (2-3 cm). Repeat after 21 days. (3) Maintain orchard hygiene: remove and burn fallen leaves and debris. (4) Band tree trunks with sticky bands to trap weevils climbing up. (5) Harvest fruit slightly early (mature green stage) and store away from orchards.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. Ina so in san yadda zan watermelon planting a aikin kankana don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da watermelon planting a aikin kankana: direct seed in field. Wannan yana taimakawa domin space 2m between rows, 1m between plants. watermelon needs full sun and well-drained soil.

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi irrigation n'ugbo tomato m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?

question: Eku oo, cowpea mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Holes in pods with frass (insect droppings) indicate pod borer (Maruca vitrata / Helicoverpa armigera). (1) Hand-pick visible caterpillars at dawn. (2) Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2 g/L in the evening — it degrades in sunlight. (3) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L, soak 12 hrs, strain) weekly. (4) Plant early-maturing varieties to escape peak pest pressure. (5) Install pheromone traps (1 per 0.1 ha) to monitor moth flights. (6) After harvest, deep-plough (20-25 cm) to expose pupae to sunlight and birds. Pre-harvest interval for Bt: 0 days (safe up to harvest day).
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. coffee na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. (3) Apply carbofuran 3G granules at 0.75 kg a.i./ha into the whorl at knee-height stage. (4) After harvest, cut stubble to ground level and bury or burn crop residues to kill overwintering larvae. (5) Rotate with legumes (cowpea, groundnut) to break the pest cycle.

question: Daalu o. oka m nwere nsogbu — shallow holes in whorl leaves with caterpillar frass. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo plantain m na-acha odo odo na ntụpọ ojii. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Dark brown streaks that enlarge to black spots on leaves indicate Black Sigatoka (Mycosphaerella fijiensis). This disease can reduce yield by 50%+. (1) Remove and destroy all heavily infected leaves — do NOT leave them on the ground. (2) Spray propiconazole at 1 ml/L OR difenoconazole at 0.5 ml/L every 14-21 days during the rainy season. ALTERNATE fungicides to prevent resistance. (3) Improve drainage — standing water increases spore production. (4) Reduce planting density for better airflow (standard: 1,700 plants/ha; reduce to 1,400 if disease is severe). (5) De-leaf weekly, leaving only 8-10 functional leaves per plant.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar cashew ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Brown, necrotic spots on leaves and dieback of young shoots indicate Tea Mosquito Bug (Helopeltis spp.). (1) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L OR quinalphos at 2 ml/L, targeting the new flush. (2) Maintain adequate shade (50-60%) — open areas suffer more damage. (3) Remove alternative host plants (especially guava, cashew) near the tea field. (4) Prune affected shoots and burn them. (5) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L as a repellent. Pre-harvest interval (plucking): lambda-cyhalothrin 7 days.

answer: Eyi je arun ti a mo si powdery mildew on watermelon. O n tan kaakiri nipase thrives in dry warm weather. plant resistant hybrid varieties. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: sulfur spray at first sign. plant resistant hybrid varieties.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, disease diagnosis advisory for watermelon farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi planting cowpea n'ugbo agwa m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka planting cowpea na agwa: sow seeds 2-3cm deep. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na space 60cm between rows, 20cm between plants. plant at start of rainy season.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi pepper nursery n'ugbo ose m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka pepper nursery na ose: start seeds in nursery. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na transplant after 6-8 weeks. space 45cm between plants, 60cm between rows.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for pepper farmers

question: E karo. Mo ri wipe epa mi ni holes in pods and root damage. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: termites lo n damu oko re. termites attack during dry periods. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: apply ash around plants. Ma gbagbe — remove woody debris from field.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for groundnut farmers

question: Ina fama da matsalar tomato ta. Ganyayyakin sun saiwoyi suna rube, ganye suna yin rawaya amma suna kore. Taya zan magance wannan?
answer: Wannan matsala ce da ke damun tomato. Ina ba da shawarar ka tuntuɓi ma'aikatar aikin gona ta gari domin ganin takamaiman maganinta. Kada ka jira — kamuwa da cuta na iya yaɗuwa cikin sauri. Allah ya sa mu dace.
source: NAERLS-Extension, general advisory for tomato farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Ahụrụ m yellow leaves and rotting trunk base na nkwu m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: basal stem rot (Ganoderma boninense) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus survives in soil and wood debris. Ngwọta: remove and burn infected trees. keep field clear of wood debris.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for oil palm farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. gawri am woodi caɗeele — chaffy grains with caterpillar inside panicle. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: millet head miner (Heliocheilus albipunctella) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. moth pest of pearl millet. Ko mbaɗata: plant early to avoid peak infestation. Woto yejjito — use resistant variety ZATIP.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for millet farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le water management fun oko iresi mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori water management fun iresi: maintain 2-5cm water depth during tillering. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe drain field 10 days before harvest. alternate wetting and drying saves water without yield loss.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for rice farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le watermelon planting fun oko gbogiri mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori watermelon planting fun gbogiri: direct seed in field. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe space 2m between rows, 1m between plants. watermelon needs full sun and well-drained soil.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for watermelon farmers

question: Barka da rana. wake ta na da matsala — curled leaves with sticky honeydew. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga cowpea aphid. aphids colonize young shoots. Magani: spray neem extract or insecticidal soap. Kada ka manta — aphids also transmit cowpea mosaic virus.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for cowpea farmers

question: E ku agba mi. Mo ri wipe anamo mi ni larvae tunnel into tubers making them bitter. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni sweet potato weevil (Cylas formicarius). adults feed on leaves and stems. Ogba: use weevil-free planting material. Mase gbagbe pe — hilling up soil around base prevents entry.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Mo ni iṣoro pẹlu plantain mi, awon ewe re are showing signs of fusarium wilt. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Eyi le jẹ ọkan ninu awọn arun ti o n kọlu plantain. Mo daba pe ki o kan si ofiisi igbimo agbe agbegbe re fun ayẹwo gangan. Mase duro pe arun le tan. Oluwa a se wa lore.
source: NAERLS-Extension, general advisory for plantain farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo ri water-soaked spots on leaves lori owu mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: bacterial blight (Xanthomonas campestris pv. malvacearum) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa bacteria spread by rain. Itoju: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for cotton farmers

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo cocoa m are showing signs of pod borer. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Nke a bụ ọrịa black pod (Phytophthora megakarya) — ọrịa kachasị njọ maka koko na West Africa. Ngwọta: wepụ mkpụrụ niile nwere ọrịa, jiri ọgwụ copper fesa, ma ghọrọ mkpụrụ chara acha n'oge.
source: NAERLS-Extension, pest/disease advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Bawo ni o. Mo ri wipe ata mi ni fruits rot from inside with maggots. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni pepper fruit fly. fly punctures fruit to lay eggs. Ogba: harvest regularly before pest builds up. Mase gbagbe pe — bag young fruits with paper.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for pepper farmers

question: Ina fama da matsalar tomato ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Fine webbing and yellow stippling on leaves indicate spider mites (Tetranychus spp.), which thrive in hot, dry conditions. (1) Spray the underside of leaves with a strong jet of water every 3 days to dislodge mites and break webbing. (2) Apply micronized sulfur at 3 g/L or abamectin at 0.5 ml/L. (3) Avoid pyrethroids and broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill predatory mites and trigger mite explosions. (4) Increase humidity around plants by mulching and watering the ground (not leaves) in the morning. (5) For heavy infestation, release Phytoseiulus persimilis predatory mites — 10/m².
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu da aiki. Na ga brown spots on leaves and stems a jikin dawa ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: anthracnose (Colletotrichum graminicola) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus survives in crop residue. Magani: rotate crops for 2 years. spray fungicide at flowering.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. Ina so in san yadda zan cocoa cultivation a aikin koko don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da cocoa cultivation a aikin koko: plant shade trees like plantain. Wannan yana taimakawa domin maintain field cleanliness regularly. spray copper fungicide for black pod prevention.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Ina kwana. Na ga dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit a jikin barkono ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: bacterial spot (Xanthomonas campestris) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar bacteria spread by rain splash. Magani: copper spray at transplanting. use disease-free seed from reliable source.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for pepper farmers

question: E ku aaro. Mo ri wipe tii mi ni shoot tips wilt and die back. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni tea mosquito bug. bug injects toxin during feeding. Ogba: shade regulation reduces population. Mase gbagbe pe — neem-based sprays for organic control.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for tea farmers

question: Ndewo. Ahụrụ m brown spots on leaves na green m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: leaf spot (Alternaria amaranthi) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus spread by rain. Ngwọta: spray copper fungicide. reduce overhead irrigation.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for amaranth farmers

question: Sannu. nyebbe am woodi caɗeele — curled leaves with sticky honeydew. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: Ɗo'o ko ñoɓɓere wi'eteende cowpea aphid. aphids colonize young shoots. Safaare: spray neem extract or insecticidal soap. Woto yejjite — aphids also transmit cowpea mosaic virus.
source: NASC-Adamawa, pest management advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi yam harvesting and storage n'ugbo ji m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka yam harvesting and storage na ji: harvest when vines dry out. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na store in well-ventilated barn. cure wounds before storage.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for yam farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i blisters on leaves turning white e shayi am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: blister blight (Exobasidium vexans) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads in misty weather. Nyawndam: spray copper fungicide. prune for good air circulation.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for tea farmers

question: Nnọọ. millet m nwere nsogbu — chaffy grains with caterpillar inside panicle. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Nke a bụ ahụhụ a na-akpọ millet head miner. moth pest of pearl millet. Ngwọta: use resistant variety ZATIP. Echefula — early planting avoids peak infestation.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, pest management advisory for millet farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i yellow leaves with V-shaped lesions e suu am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: black rot (Xanthomonas campestris) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e bacteria spread by water. Nyawndam: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 3 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. okwuru m nwere nsogbu — small round holes in leaves like shot pattern. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: okra flea beetle (Podagrica uniforma) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. heavy infestation defoliates young plants. Ihe ị ga-eme: neem oil spray and ash dusting. Echefula — plant early to escape peak beetle season.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for okra farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. Mi yi'i diamond-shaped gray lesions on leaves e marori am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: rice blast (Pyricularia oryzae) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungal spores carried by wind. Nyawndam: use resistant varieties like FARO 44. excess nitrogen makes blast worse.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for rice farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo ri diamond-shaped gray lesions on leaves lori iresi mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: rice blast (Pyricularia oryzae) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungal spores carried by wind. Itoju: use resistant varieties like FARO 44. excess nitrogen makes blast worse.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for rice farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. Na ga white powdery coating on leaves a jikin kuɓewa ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: powdery mildew ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus spreads in dry season. Magani: spray sulfur fungicide. remove infected leaves.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for okra farmers

question: No wa'i. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta tea planting e ndemri shayi am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow tea planting e shayi: plant on well-drained slopes. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 1.5m between plants. prune regularly to encourage new growth.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for tea farmers

question: Daalu o. ose m nwere nsogbu — fruits rot from inside with maggots. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Nke a bụ ahụhụ a na-akpọ pepper fruit fly. fly punctures fruit to lay eggs. Ngwọta: harvest regularly before pest builds up. Echefula — bag young fruits with paper.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, pest management advisory for pepper farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. yorobo m nwere nsogbu — silvery streaks and twisted leaves. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: onion thrips (Thrips tabaci) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. thrips suck plant sap. Ihe ị ga-eme: spray insecticidal soap. Echefula — plant onions away from other allium fields.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for onion farmers

question: Jam na. Mi yi'i white powdery coating on leaves e la'ano am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: powdery mildew woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads in dry season. Nyawndam: spray sulfur fungicide. remove infected leaves.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for okra farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo fe mo bi mo se le oil palm care fun oko ope mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori oil palm care fun ope: apply NPK 15-15-15 annually. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe prune dead fronds regularly. clear area around trees to reduce pests.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for oil palm farmers

question: Nebbe am ndanɗi na nawa kadi himbe na njeewi. Ko waɗi?
answer: Nebbe ɗe ndanɗi (beans weevils) ko torra mawnde e nder cuuɗi. (1) Yooru nebbe ɗen e naange haa selli ko adii ɗaɗanaaki. (2) Huutoro neem oil (5ml e nder litru 1). (3) Wintoo nder cuuɗi ɗi henndu naatataa. (4) Nebbe ɗen wintoo nder friisa (freezer) balɗe 7 — himbe ɗen maɓe maaya. (5) Lartu cuuɗi ɗi ɗaɗanotonoo. (6) Yeewtu e ofisaajo demal (ADP) ngam heɓde gabbe ɗe himbe njiɗataa.
source: ADP Fulfulde Cowpea Guide; IITA Post-Harvest

question: E ku agba mi. Mo ri wipe isu mi ni holes bored into tubers reducing market value. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni yam beetle. adult beetles feed at night. Ogba: deep planting (15cm) reduces damage. Mase gbagbe pe — mulching with neem leaves repels beetles.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for yam farmers

question: Eku oo, mo ri pe awon ewe cowpea mi ti n are showing signs of aphids. Kini ohun ti mo le se lati gba to?
answer: Eyi je kokoro aphid (kokoro kekere ti o n fa oje eweko). Aphid n tan arun kaakiri. Imoran: gbin ni kutukutu ki o to akoko ti aphid yoo po, tabi lo epo neem. Gba irugbin ti ko ni arun lati odo ile-ise iwadi ogbin.
source: NAERLS-Extension, pest/disease advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Barka dai. Ina so in san yadda zan amaranth planting a aikin alaiho don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da amaranth planting a aikin alaiho: broadcast seeds on prepared bed. Wannan yana taimakawa domin water regularly. harvest after 4-6 weeks.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for amaranth farmers

question: Ezigbo ohi. Ahụrụ m white powder on leaves reducing photosynthesis na watermelon m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ọrịa a na-akpọ powdery mildew on watermelon. Ọ na-agbasa site na thrives in dry warm weather. plant resistant hybrid varieties. Ihe ị ga-eme: sulfur spray at first sign. plant resistant hybrid varieties.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for watermelon farmers

question: Ina fama da matsalar cabbage ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Seedlings cut at ground level overnight indicate cutworm (Agrotis spp.). (1) Hand-pick cutworms from the soil surface at night using a torch — they hide in the top 2-3 cm of soil during the day and come up to feed at night. (2) Place collars around seedlings: cut the bottom from a plastic cup or use a cardboard tube pushed 2 cm into the soil. (3) Apply neem cake at 50 g per square metre around plants — it deters egg-laying. (4) Sprinkle wood ash in a ring around each plant. (5) Plough the field 2-3 weeks before planting to expose larvae to birds.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: E ku ise. Mo ri wipe kabeji mi ni small holes in leaves and green larvae. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: diamondback moth (Plutella xylostella) lo n damu oko re. moth lays eggs on leaf undersides. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis). Ma gbagbe — rotate crops to break life cycle.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Sannu da zuwa. gero ta na da matsala — chaffy grains with caterpillar inside panicle. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga millet head miner. moth pest of pearl millet. Magani: use resistant variety ZATIP. Kada ka manta — early planting avoids peak infestation.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for millet farmers

question: Awon eso watermelon mi ti n fo lori oko. Kini o nfa eyi?
answer: Awon eso watermelon ti o fo lori oko le je nitori (1) Iyato ninu omi - rii pe o n fi omi kun ni gbogbo igba. (2) Aini calcium - fi gypsum tabi calcium nitrate si ile. (3) Arun blossom-end rot - wo calcium deficiency. (4) Ki o ma fi omi kun ju ni igba kan ati pe ki omi ma ni fo pelu ibaje. (5) Rii pe pH ile wa ni aarin 6.0-6.5. (6) Gbin iru eso ti o le fa: Kaolack, Crimson Sweet. (7) Lo mulch lati da omi duro ni ile.
source: IITA Watermelon Guide; ADP Fruit Cracking Advisory

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri dark spots on leaves and vine dieback lori isu mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: yam anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spreads in rainy season. Itoju: use resistant variety TDr 95/19177. avoid planting in waterlogged soil.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for yam farmers

question: Sannu. koko ta na da matsala — feeding lesions on pods and shoots. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: cocoa mirids (Sahlbergella singularis) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. mirids inject toxic saliva. Abin da za ka yi: spray bifenthrin at recommended rates. Kada ka manta — shade management reduces mirid population.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Nnọọ. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi onion planting n'ugbo yorobo m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka onion planting na yorobo: direct seed or use nursery transplants. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na space 20cm between rows, 10cm between plants. onions need full sun exposure.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for onion farmers

question: Ina kwana. Na ga sores in mouth and on hooves a jikin kiwo ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: foot and mouth disease (FMD) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar highly contagious viral disease. Magani: isolate infected animals. call veterinarian immediately.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for dairy farmers

question: Ek'abo. Mo ri wipe iresi mi ni central shoot drying out — deadheart symptom. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: rice stem borer lo n damu oko re. moth larvae bore into stem. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: apply carbofuran granules at panicle initiation. Ma gbagbe — fields near wild grasses have higher infestation.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for rice farmers

question: Ezigbo ohi. ji m nwere nsogbu — holes bored into tubers reducing market value. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Nke a bụ ahụhụ a na-akpọ yam beetle. adult beetles feed at night. Ngwọta: deep planting (15cm) reduces damage. Echefula — mulching with neem leaves repels beetles.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, pest management advisory for yam farmers

question: Sannu. Mi yi'i white powdery coating on leaves e la'ano am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: powdery mildew woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads in dry season. Nyawndam: spray sulfur fungicide. remove infected leaves.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for okra farmers

question: Gawri am (millet) na mboddi, ko torra?
answer: Gawri mbodɗi ko downy mildew. (1) Lartu gawri nde mbaayi — suna. (2) Demoo gabbe ɗe ngooɗata: 'Ex-Borno', 'LCIC 9702', 'SOSAT-C88'. (3) Naatin gabbe e ndiyam ngulmam (52°C) miniti 10. (4) Luurtin ndema. (5) Demoo ko adii — gawri yidani ko adii. (6) Yeewtu e ADP ngam fungicide.
source: ADP Millet Downy Mildew Guide; ICRISAT Millet Control

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown lori ere mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: cowpea bacterial blight lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa rain splash spreads bacteria. Itoju: apply copper-based fungicide. use certified disease-free seed.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Sannu. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta mango tree care e ndemri mangoro am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow mango tree care e mangoro: prune dead branches annually. Ɗum wallitata sabo apply organic fertilizer around base. irrigate during dry season.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for mango farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi millet planting n'ugbo millet m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka millet planting na millet: broadcast or plant in rows. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na millet is highly drought-tolerant. plant at start of rains for good yield.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for millet farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo ri wipe ogede mi ni larvae tunnel into corm causing toppling. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: banana weevil (Cosmopolites sordidus) lo n damu oko re. adults hide in crop residues. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: use clean planting material (tissue culture). Ma gbagbe — trap adults with pseudostem discs.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for plantain farmers

question: E ku ise o. Mo ri wipe tete mi ni caterpillar webs leaves together and feeds inside. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni amaranth leaf webber. pest of leafy amaranth vegetables. Ogba: hand-pick and destroy webbed leaves. Mase gbagbe pe — neem spray prevents egg laying.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for amaranth farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo ri orange powdery dust on undersides of leaves lori kofi mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: coffee leaf rust (Hemileia vastatrix) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spread by wind. Itoju: spray copper fungicide. plant resistant varieties.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for coffee farmers

question: Nnọọ. Ahụrụ m yellow and white streaked leaves na millet m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: downy mildew (Sclerospora graminicola) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus spread by wind and rain. Ngwọta: use resistant varieties. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for millet farmers

question: Ina kwana. Na ga orange powdery dust on undersides of leaves a jikin kofi ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: coffee leaf rust (Hemileia vastatrix) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus spread by wind. Magani: spray copper fungicide. plant resistant varieties.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for coffee farmers

question: No wa'i. Mi yi'i brown streaks inside tubers e rogo am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: cassava brown streak disease woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e spread by whiteflies and infected cuttings. Nyawndam: uproot and burn infected plants. makes tubers bitter and inedible.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for cassava farmers

question: Sannu da zuwa. cowpea na ya are showing signs of thrips. Me zan yi don gba to?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga aphid (ƙwarin ƙwaya). Aphids suna tsotse ruwan ganye suna kuma ɗauke da ƙwayoyin cuta. Magani: shuka da wuri kafin lokacin aphid ya ƙaru, ko kuma a yi spraying da neem oil. Ɗauki kayan gona daga cibiyar noma ta gida don shawara mai kyau.
source: NAERLS-Extension, pest/disease advisory for cowpea farmers

question: E pele o. Mo ri discolored grains with fungal growth lori baba mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: Eyi je arun ti a mo si grain mold. O n tan kaakiri nipase high humidity at grain filling. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: harvest at physiological maturity. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, disease diagnosis advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. shayi ta na da matsala — dark spots on leaves and young shoots. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: tea mosquito bug (Helopeltis antonii) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. bug pierces leaves and sucks sap. Abin da za ka yi: spray neem oil. Kada ka manta — prune affected branches.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for tea farmers

question: Ek'abo. Mo fe mo bi mo se le cashew planting fun oko kasu mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori cashew planting fun kasu: plant trees 10m apart. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe apply organic fertilizer. prune dead branches regularly.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for cashew farmers

question: Eku oo, sorghum mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Dead central shoot ('dead heart') in young seedlings indicates shoot fly (Atherigona soccata). (1) Remove and destroy affected seedlings. (2) Apply carbofuran granules at 1 kg a.i./ha in the seed furrow at planting. (3) Sow early at the onset of rains — late-sown crops suffer more damage. (4) Use higher seed rate (12 kg/ha instead of 8) and thin later — this compensates for losses. (5) Apply neem cake at 250 kg/ha at planting. (6) Avoid excessive nitrogen top-dressing during the seedling stage.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ek'abo. Mo fe mo bi mo se le onion planting fun oko alubosa mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori onion planting fun alubosa: direct seed or use nursery transplants. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe space 20cm between rows, 10cm between plants. onions need full sun exposure.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for onion farmers

question: Sannu. sunflower ta na da matsala — larvae in sunflower head feeding on seeds. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: head moth (Homoeosoma electellum) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. moth lays eggs on flowers. Abin da za ka yi: spray Bt at flowering. Kada ka manta — plant resistant varieties.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for sunflower farmers

question: Mawɗe am na mari koyngol (smut) ɓale. Ko waɗi?
answer: Koyngol ɓale ko sorghum smut. (1) Lartu mawɗe ɗe mbaayɗe — suna ko adii ɗe mbaɗtora. (2) Demoo gabbe ɗe ngooɗata: 'Seredo', 'Macia', 'Gadam'. (3) Naatin gabbe ɗen e ndiyam ɗam ngulmam (52°C) miniti 10 ko adii ndema. (4) Huutoro seed dressing — ADP yeɗata. (5) Luurtin ndema. (6) Woto a huutoro azote ɗuuɗuka.
source: ADP Sorghum Smut Guide; ICRISAT Smut Management

question: Ek'abo. Mo fe mo bi mo se le oil palm care fun oko ope mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori oil palm care fun ope: apply NPK 15-15-15 annually. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe prune dead fronds regularly. clear area around trees to reduce pests.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for oil palm farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. nduku m nwere nsogbu — holes in tubers with bitter taste. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: sweet potato weevil (Cylas puncticollis) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. weevil attacks underground. Ihe ị ga-eme: hill soil to cover exposed tubers. Echefula — rotate crops for 2 years.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Barka dai. Na ga white powder on flowers and leaves a jikin kanju ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: powdery mildew ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus prevents fruit set. Magani: spray sulfur fungicide. prune for good air circulation.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for cashew farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi sweet potato planting n'ugbo nduku m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka sweet potato planting na nduku: plant healthy vines 25-30cm long. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na space 1m between rows, 30cm between plants. plant at start of rainy season.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. Ina so in san yadda zan cashew planting a aikin kanju don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da cashew planting a aikin kanju: plant trees 10m apart. Wannan yana taimakawa domin apply organic fertilizer. prune dead branches regularly.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for cashew farmers

question: Ina fama da matsalar millet ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Orange-brown powdery pustules on leaves indicate rust (Puccinia spp.). (1) Spray propiconazole at 1 ml/L OR tebuconazole at 0.5 ml/L at first sign. (2) Plant resistant varieties where available. (3) Avoid excessive nitrogen — it promotes lush, susceptible growth. (4) Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest. (5) Practice early planting to avoid peak rust season. (6) Apply balanced NPK (not just urea) to strengthen cell walls.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: E ku ise. Mo fe mo bi mo se le weeding schedule fun oko pakí mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori weeding schedule fun pakí: first weeding 3 weeks after planting, second at 8 weeks. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe competing weeds reduce yield by 40%. maintain clean field throughout growth.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for cassava farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri yellow leaves with white underside lori sunflower mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: downy mildew lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus survives in soil. Itoju: use resistant varieties. rotate crops for 3 years.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for sunflower farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo ri angular brown spots on leaves lori ere mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: angular leaf spot lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spread by rain splash. Itoju: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for beans farmers

question: Kedu. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi pepper nursery n'ugbo ose m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka pepper nursery na ose: start seeds in nursery. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na transplant after 6-8 weeks. space 45cm between plants, 60cm between rows.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for pepper farmers

question: Mo ni isoro pelu oil palm mi, awon ewe re ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Emi ko le fun e ni idahun pato nipa oil palm re lati inu apejuwe yi nikan. Awon orisirisi isoro le farahan bira won. Jowo mu ayewo ewe ati gbongbo lo si ibudo ise agbe ti o sunmo e, tabi pe agronomist agbegbe fun ayewo gidi.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i brown spots on leaves e biriiji am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: early leaf spot (Cercospora arachidicola) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus survives in crop residue. Nyawndam: spray fungicide at first appearance. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for groundnut farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi banana planting n'ugbo unere m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka banana planting na unere: plant healthy suckers 30cm deep. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na space 3m between plants. water regularly during dry season.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for banana farmers

question: No wa'i. Mi yi'i yellow and white streaked leaves e gawri am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: downy mildew (Sclerospora graminicola) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spread by wind and rain. Nyawndam: use resistant varieties. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for millet farmers

question: Ina kwana. dabino ta na da matsala — larvae tunnel into trunk weakening the tree. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga palm weevil (Rhynchophorus phoenicis). adults attracted to wounds on trunk. Magani: avoid wounding trunk during pruning. Kada ka manta — pheromone traps for monitoring.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for oil palm farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. Ina so in san yadda zan cocoa cultivation a aikin koko don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da cocoa cultivation a aikin koko: plant shade trees like plantain. Wannan yana taimakawa domin maintain field cleanliness regularly. spray copper fungicide for black pod prevention.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for cocoa farmers

question: E karo. Mo fe mo bi mo se le sorghum planting fun oko baba mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori sorghum planting fun baba: sow seeds 3-5cm deep. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe space 75cm between rows, 20cm between plants. sorghum tolerates drought better than maize.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Jam na. tamaro am woodi caɗeele — larvae tunnel into trunk weakening the tree. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: palm weevil (Rhynchophorus phoenicis) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. adults attracted to wounds on trunk. Ko mbaɗata: avoid wounding trunk during pruning. Woto yejjito — pheromone traps for monitoring.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for oil palm farmers

question: No wa'i. Mi yi'i yellow stunted leaves e dankali am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: sweet potato virus disease (SPVD) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e spread by whiteflies and aphids. Nyawndam: use virus-free vines. remove infected plants.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Sannu. shayi ta na da matsala — shoot tips wilt and die back. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga tea mosquito bug. bug injects toxin during feeding. Magani: shade regulation reduces population. Kada ka manta — neem-based sprays for organic control.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for tea farmers

question: Ndewo. mmiri ara m nwere nsogbu — ticks on cattle body sucking blood. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: ticks (Rhipicephalus microplus) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. ticks transmit diseases like East Coast fever. Ihe ị ga-eme: dip or spray cattle with acaricide every 2 weeks. Echefula — maintain clean grazing areas to reduce ticks.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for dairy farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. sunflower ta na da matsala — larvae in sunflower head feeding on seeds. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?

question: Nnọọ. mmiri ara m nwere nsogbu — ticks on cattle body sucking blood. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: ticks (Rhipicephalus microplus) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. ticks transmit diseases like East Coast fever. Ihe ị ga-eme: dip or spray cattle with acaricide every 2 weeks. Echefula — maintain clean grazing areas to reduce ticks.

question: E ku ise. Mo ri wipe isu mi ni holes bored into tubers reducing market value. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: yam beetle (Heteroligus meles) lo n damu oko re. adult beetles feed at night. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: deep planting (15cm) reduces damage. Ma gbagbe — mulching with neem leaves repels beetles.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for yam farmers

question: No wa'i. Mi yi'i dark spots on ripening fruit e mangoro am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads via rain splash. Nyawndam: spray fungicide before harvest. hot water dip after harvest.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for mango farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. tumatir ta na da matsala — mines inside leaves leaving transparent patches. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: tomato leaf miner (Tuta absoluta) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. moth pest spreads rapidly. Abin da za ka yi: use pheromone traps and neem spray. Kada ka manta — can destroy whole field in 2 weeks without control.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for tomato farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. Na ga purple-brown lesions on leaves that girdle them a jikin albasa ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira onion purple blotch. Yana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus Alternaria porri. rotate away from allium fields for 3 years. Abin yi: spray mancozeb at 10-day intervals. rotate away from allium fields for 3 years.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for onion farmers

question: Sannu da zuwa. alaiho ta na da matsala — caterpillar webs leaves together and feeds inside. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga amaranth leaf webber. pest of leafy amaranth vegetables. Magani: hand-pick and destroy webbed leaves. Kada ka manta — neem spray prevents egg laying.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for amaranth farmers

question: Jam na. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta mango tree care e ndemri mangoro am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow mango tree care e mangoro: prune dead branches annually. Ɗum wallitata sabo apply organic fertilizer around base. irrigate during dry season.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for mango farmers

question: Barka dai. Ina so in san yadda zan tea planting a aikin shayi don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da tea planting a aikin shayi: plant on well-drained slopes. Wannan yana taimakawa domin space 1.5m between plants. prune regularly to encourage new growth.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for tea farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown e nyebbe am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: cowpea bacterial blight woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e rain splash spreads bacteria. Nyawndam: apply copper-based fungicide. use certified disease-free seed.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for cowpea farmers

question: No wa'i. Mi yi'i dark spots on leaves and vine dieback e dundu am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: yam anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads in rainy season. Nyawndam: use resistant variety TDr 95/19177. avoid planting in waterlogged soil.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for yam farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. Ina so in san yadda zan mango tree care a aikin mangwaro don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da mango tree care a aikin mangwaro: prune dead branches annually. Wannan yana taimakawa domin apply organic fertilizer around base. irrigate during dry season.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for mango farmers

question: Kedu. Ahụrụ m yellow leaves with white underside na sunflower m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: downy mildew na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus survives in soil. Ngwọta: use resistant varieties. rotate crops for 3 years.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for sunflower farmers

question: Sannu. Mi yi'i mosaic yellow-green patterns on leaves e rogo am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: Ɗo'o ko rafi wi'eteedo cassava mosaic virus (CMD). O saakotoo e laawol whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci). infected plants produce small tubers. Ko potɗaa waɗde: use CMD-resistant varieties like TME 419. infected plants produce small tubers.
source: NASC-Adamawa, disease diagnosis advisory for cassava farmers

question: Ina kwana. Ina so in san yadda zan tea planting a aikin shayi don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da tea planting a aikin shayi: plant on well-drained slopes. Wannan yana taimakawa domin space 1.5m between plants. prune regularly to encourage new growth.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for tea farmers

question: Sannu. Ina so in san yadda zan harvesting and storage a aikin wake don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da harvesting and storage a aikin wake: harvest when pods are dry. Wannan yana taimakawa domin store in airtight PICS bags. protect from bruchid weevils in storage.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Sannu da zuwa. wake ta na da matsala — curled leaves with sticky honeydew. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga cowpea aphid. aphids colonize young shoots. Magani: spray neem extract or insecticidal soap. Kada ka manta — aphids also transmit cowpea mosaic virus.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Sannu. Ina so in san yadda zan okra planting a aikin kuɓewa don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da okra planting a aikin kuɓewa: sow seeds 2-3cm deep. Wannan yana taimakawa domin space 60cm between rows, 30cm between plants. okra needs full sun and well-drained soil.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for okra farmers

question: Maalu mi (dairy cow) nso wara kekere. Kini iṣoro?
answer: Maalu ti o nso wara kekere le ni ọpọlọpọ awọn okunfa. (1) Ounjẹ — fun ni koriko didara, dairy meal 2-3 kg lojoojumọ. (2) Omi — maalu nilo omi 40-60 lita lojoojumọ. (3) Ilera — ṣayẹwo ti o ba ni mastitis tabi aisan miiran. (4) Iru (breed) — Friesian, Jersey, Sokoto Gudali dara fun wara. (5) Ọjọ ori — maalu agbalagba nso wara kekere. (6) Kan si dokita eranko (vet).
source: NAERLS Dairy Guide; DVS Milk Production

question: Ndewo. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi water management n'ugbo osikapa m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka water management na osikapa: maintain 2-5cm water depth during tillering. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na drain field 10 days before harvest. alternate wetting and drying saves water without yield loss.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for rice farmers

question: Kedu. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi watermelon planting n'ugbo watermelon m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka watermelon planting na watermelon: direct seed in field. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na space 2m between rows, 1m between plants. watermelon needs full sun and well-drained soil.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for watermelon farmers

question: Ina kwana. wake ta na da matsala — holes in pods with frass inside. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: pod borer (Maruca vitrata) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. moth lays eggs on flowers. Abin da za ka yi: spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at flowering. Kada ka manta — one larva destroys 4-6 pods in its lifetime.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Sannu. groundnut na suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Me zan yi?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near groundnut to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Nnọọ. agwa m nwere nsogbu — stunted plants with yellow leaves. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: bean fly (Ophiomyia phaseoli) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. fly larvae bore into stems. Ihe ị ga-eme: plant early to escape peak fly season. Echefula — apply mulch around plants.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for beans farmers

question: No wa'i. tumate am woodi caɗeele — mines inside leaves leaving transparent patches. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?

question: Mbaaɗa. suu am woodi caɗeele — small holes in leaves and green larvae. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: diamondback moth (Plutella xylostella) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. moth lays eggs on leaf undersides. Ko mbaɗata: spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis). Woto yejjito — rotate crops to break life cycle.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Ndewo. Ahụrụ m yellow leaves with white underside na sunflower m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
