question: Ndewo. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi watermelon planting n'ugbo watermelon m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka watermelon planting na watermelon: direct seed in field. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na space 2m between rows, 1m between plants. watermelon needs full sun and well-drained soil.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for watermelon farmers

question: Nnọọ. nduku m nwere nsogbu — larvae tunnel into tubers making them bitter. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Nke a bụ ahụhụ a na-akpọ sweet potato weevil (Cylas formicarius). adults feed on leaves and stems. Ngwọta: use weevil-free planting material. Echefula — hilling up soil around base prevents entry.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: A wali. Mi yi'i white powdery coating on flowers and young fruit e mango am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: Ɗo'o ko rafi wi'eteedo powdery mildew. O saakotoo e laawol fungus loves warm humid air. prune for good air circulation. Ko potɗaa waɗde: spray sulfur-based fungicide at flowering. prune for good air circulation.
source: NASC-Adamawa, disease diagnosis advisory for mango farmers

question: Daalunu. cowpea m nwere obere ahụhụ na akwụkwọ. Gini ka m ga-eme?
answer: Stunted growth, yellowing, swollen root galls (knots), and wilting despite moist soil indicate root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). (1) There is no curative chemical treatment. (2) Incorporate fresh neem leaves or neem cake at 500 kg/ha into the soil 2 weeks before the next planting. (3) Solarize the soil with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks. (4) Plant marigold (Tagetes erecta) as a trap crop — its roots release natural nematicides. (5) Rotate with maize, sorghum, or millet for 2-3 seasons — these are non-hosts. (6) Apply well-composted manure at 5 t/ha; the microbial activity suppresses nematodes.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mbaaɗa. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta pepper nursery e ndemri citta am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow pepper nursery e citta: start seeds in nursery. Ɗum wallitata sabo transplant after 6-8 weeks. space 45cm between plants, 60cm between rows.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for pepper farmers

question: Jam na. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta yam planting e ndemri dundu am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow yam planting e dundu: use healthy tuber setts 500g-800g. Ɗum wallitata sabo build mounds 1m apart. apply mulch to conserve moisture.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for yam farmers

question: Eku oo, cocoa mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: Dense clusters of small, distorted shoots ('witches' brooms') indicate Witches' Broom Disease caused by Moniliophthora perniciosa. (1) Prune and burn ALL brooms and infected branches — cut at least 15 cm BELOW the visible broom into healthy wood. (2) Remove diseased pods. (3) Apply copper oxychloride at 3 g/L during flowering to protect new pods. (4) Maintain 40-50% shade — full sun exposure stresses trees and increases susceptibility. (5) Plant resistant cultivars where available (e.g., TSH series). (6) Disinfect pruning tools with 10% bleach solution between trees.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. cotton m nwere nsogbu — larvae bore into bolls causing them to drop. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: cotton bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. polyphagous pest — also attacks tomato and maize. Ihe ị ga-eme: Bt cotton provides genetic resistance. Echefula — spray neem kernel extract at flowering.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for cotton farmers

question: No wa'i. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta rice planting e ndemri marori am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow rice planting e marori: plant in rows 20cm apart. Ɗum wallitata sabo prepare field thoroughly before planting. plant at start of rainy season for best results.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for rice farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. Ina so in san yadda zan proper maize spacing a aikin masara don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da proper maize spacing a aikin masara: space rows 75cm apart, plants 25cm apart. Wannan yana taimakawa domin gives enough light and air. reduces competition between plants for nutrients.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for maize farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. shinkafa ta na da matsala — central shoot drying out — deadheart symptom. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: rice stem borer ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. moth larvae bore into stem. Abin da za ka yi: apply carbofuran granules at panicle initiation. Kada ka manta — fields near wild grasses have higher infestation.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for rice farmers

question: Ina kwana. gero ta na da matsala — chaffy grains with caterpillar inside panicle. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga millet head miner. moth pest of pearl millet. Magani: use resistant variety ZATIP. Kada ka manta — early planting avoids peak infestation.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for millet farmers

question: E karo. Mo ri dark streaks on leaves reducing photosynthesis lori ogede mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: black sigatoka (Mycosphaerella fijiensis) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spread by wind. Itoju: spray fungicide regularly. remove infected leaves.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for plantain farmers

question: Jam na. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta millet planting e ndemri gawri am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow millet planting e gawri: broadcast or plant in rows. Ɗum wallitata sabo millet is highly drought-tolerant. plant at start of rains for good yield.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for millet farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i pods turn black with white flour-like coating e koko am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: black pod disease (Phytophthora megakarya) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e most serious cocoa disease in West Africa. Nyawndam: remove infected pods and spray copper fungicide. harvest ripe pods promptly — delay increases rot.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. Ina so in san yadda zan grazing rotation a aikin kiwo don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da grazing rotation a aikin kiwo: rotate grazing areas every week. Wannan yana taimakawa domin allow pasture to rest between grazing. this prevents overgrazing and reduces disease.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for dairy farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i dark spots on leaves and vine dieback e dundu am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: yam anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads in rainy season. Nyawndam: use resistant variety TDr 95/19177. avoid planting in waterlogged soil.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for yam farmers

question: Nnọọ. Ahụrụ m dark spots on leaves and vine dieback na ji m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: yam anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus spreads in rainy season. Ngwọta: use resistant variety TDr 95/19177. avoid planting in waterlogged soil.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for yam farmers

question: Sannu. Na ga yellow streaks on leaves a jikin masara ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: maize streak virus (MSV) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar spread by leafhoppers. Magani: remove infected plants early. no cure once plant is infected.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for maize farmers

question: No wa'i. ayaba am woodi caɗeele — curled leaves with aphids underneath. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. aphids transmit bunchy top virus. Ko mbaɗata: spray insecticidal soap. Woto yejjito — remove infected plants.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for banana farmers

question: E ku aaro. Mo ri purple-brown lesions on leaves that girdle them lori alubosa mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: Eyi je arun ti a mo si onion purple blotch. O n tan kaakiri nipase fungus Alternaria porri. rotate away from allium fields for 3 years. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: spray mancozeb at 10-day intervals. rotate away from allium fields for 3 years.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, disease diagnosis advisory for onion farmers

question: No wa'i. Mi yi'i dark spots on leaves and vine dieback e dundu am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: yam anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads in rainy season. Nyawndam: use resistant variety TDr 95/19177. avoid planting in waterlogged soil.

question: Eku agba mi, millet mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grey-purple fuzz underneath indicate downy mildew (Peronospora spp.). (1) Spray metalaxyl-M + mancozeb at 2 g/L OR phosphorous acid at 3 ml/L every 7-10 days. (2) Improve field drainage and air circulation. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening — water early morning instead. (4) Remove crop debris after harvest. (5) Use disease-free seed for the next planting. (6) For onion, cure bulbs properly (7-10 days in sun) before storage.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mbaaɗa. marori am woodi caɗeele — central shoot drying out — deadheart symptom. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: rice stem borer woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. moth larvae bore into stem. Ko mbaɗata: apply carbofuran granules at panicle initiation. Woto yejjito — fields near wild grasses have higher infestation.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for rice farmers

question: No wa'i. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta grazing rotation e ndemri kossam am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow grazing rotation e kossam: rotate grazing areas every week. Ɗum wallitata sabo allow pasture to rest between grazing. this prevents overgrazing and reduces disease.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for dairy farmers

question: Sannu. kuɓewa ta na da matsala — small round holes in leaves like shot pattern. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga okra flea beetle. heavy infestation defoliates young plants. Magani: neem oil spray and ash dusting. Kada ka manta — plant early to escape peak beetle season.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for okra farmers

question: Eku agba mi, tomato mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Dark spots on leaves with white fungal growth on the underside and rotting fruit indicate late blight (Phytophthora infestans). This disease can destroy a field within DAYS in wet weather. (1) Spray mancozeb (2.5 g/L) OR metalaxyl-M + mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) at 2 g/L, alternating every 7 days. (2) Improve staking and pruning so leaves don't touch soil. (3) NEVER work in the field when leaves are wet. (4) Remove and bury infected plant material away from the field. (5) Plant resistant varieties like Rio Grande or Roma VF. (6) Apply mulch to reduce rain splash. Pre-harvest interval for mancozeb: 5 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: A salaamun alaikum. kankana am woodi caɗeele — larvae inside fruit causing rot. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: melon fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. fly punctures fruit to lay eggs. Ko mbaɗata: cover young fruits with paper bags. Woto yejjito — harvest early before pest builds up.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for watermelon farmers

question: Sannu. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta sunflower planting e ndemri sunflower am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow sunflower planting e sunflower: sow seeds 2-3cm deep. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 75cm between rows, 30cm between plants. sunflower needs full sun.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for sunflower farmers

question: Daalunu. okra m nwere obere ahụhụ na akwụkwọ. Gini ka m ga-eme?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo cowpea m na-acha odo odo na ntụpọ ojii. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near cowpea to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Assalamu alaikum. Na ga water-soaked spots on leaves and pods a jikin wake ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: common bacterial blight ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar bacteria spread by rain. Magani: do not work in field when leaves are wet. plant resistant varieties.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for beans farmers

question: Sannu. Na ga leaves become narrow and bunched at top a jikin ayaba ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira banana bunchy top virus. Yana yaduwa ta hanyar aphid-transmitted, no cure. use virus-free suckers from certified source. Abin yi: uproot and destroy infected plants. use virus-free suckers from certified source.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for banana farmers

question: Sannu. Na ga dark spots on leaves and vine dieback a jikin doya ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: yam anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus spreads in rainy season. Magani: use resistant variety TDr 95/19177. avoid planting in waterlogged soil.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for yam farmers

question: Eku oo, maize mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini mo le se?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. (3) Apply carbofuran 3G granules at 0.75 kg a.i./ha into the whorl at knee-height stage. (4) After harvest, cut stubble to ground level and bury or burn crop residues to kill overwintering larvae. (5) Rotate with legumes (cowpea, groundnut) to break the pest cycle.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu da aiki. mangwaro ta na da matsala — small puncture marks on fruit with larvae inside. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga mango fruit fly. female fly lays eggs under skin. Magani: use pheromone traps (methyl eugenol). Kada ka manta — collect fallen fruits and bury deep.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for mango farmers

question: Barka dai. dankali ta na da matsala — holes in tubers with bitter taste. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: sweet potato weevil (Cylas puncticollis) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. weevil attacks underground. Abin da za ka yi: hill soil to cover exposed tubers. Kada ka manta — rotate crops for 2 years.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Sannu. Na ga diamond-shaped gray lesions on leaves a jikin shinkafa ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: rice blast (Pyricularia oryzae) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungal spores carried by wind. Magani: use resistant varieties like FARO 44. excess nitrogen makes blast worse.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for rice farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta amaranth planting e ndemri kohi am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow amaranth planting e kohi: broadcast seeds on prepared bed. Ɗum wallitata sabo water regularly. harvest after 4-6 weeks.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for amaranth farmers

question: Jam na. biriiji am woodi caɗeele — stunted plants with curled yellow leaves. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: Ɗo'o ko ñoɓɓere wi'eteende groundnut aphid. aphids vector rosette virus. Safaare: early planting avoids peak aphid season. Woto yejjite — neem seed extract spray.
source: NASC-Adamawa, pest management advisory for groundnut farmers

question: Sannu. kofi ta na da matsala — small holes in coffee berries with damage inside. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga coffee berry borer (Hypothenemus hampei). most serious coffee pest globally. Magani: harvest all ripe berries promptly. Kada ka manta — use broca traps with ethanol-methanol mix.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for coffee farmers

question: Eku oo, cabbage mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini mo le se?
answer: Seedlings cut at ground level overnight indicate cutworm (Agrotis spp.). (1) Hand-pick cutworms from the soil surface at night using a torch — they hide in the top 2-3 cm of soil during the day and come up to feed at night. (2) Place collars around seedlings: cut the bottom from a plastic cup or use a cardboard tube pushed 2 cm into the soil. (3) Apply neem cake at 50 g per square metre around plants — it deters egg-laying. (4) Sprinkle wood ash in a ring around each plant. (5) Plough the field 2-3 weeks before planting to expose larvae to birds.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ek'abo. Mo fe mo bi mo se le cabbage planting fun oko kabeji mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori cabbage planting fun kabeji: start seeds in nursery. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe transplant after 4-5 weeks. space 45cm between plants.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Ina fama da matsalar cassava ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: This is cassava whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Do NOT spray broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill natural enemies like Encarsia wasps and make outbreaks worse. Instead: (1) Spray insecticidal soap or 0.5% neem oil solution every 7 days for 3 weeks. (2) Remove and burn heavily infested leaves. (3) Plant maize or sorghum as barrier crops between cassava rows to disrupt whitefly movement. (4) Use yellow sticky traps (1 per 10 m²). If infestation persists, apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L as a LAST resort, observing a 14-day pre-harvest interval. Wash hands and produce after application.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu da aiki. Ina so in san yadda zan sunflower planting a aikin sunflower don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da sunflower planting a aikin sunflower: sow seeds 2-3cm deep. Wannan yana taimakawa domin space 75cm between rows, 30cm between plants. sunflower needs full sun.

question: A salaamun alaikum. Mi yi'i yellow leaves and rotting trunk base e tamaro am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?

question: Sannu. suu am woodi caɗeele — small holes in leaves and green larvae. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?

question: Assalamu alaikum. Na ga yellow stunted leaves a jikin dankali ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?

question: Gawri am (millet) na sewi, koyɗe na mboddi. Ko torra?

question: E ku aaro. Mo ri wipe kofi mi ni small holes in coffee berries with damage inside. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?

question: Ina fama da matsalar maize ta. Ganyayyakin sun ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Yellowing of lower leaves (starting at the tip and moving inward in a V shape on maize) indicates nitrogen deficiency. (1) Apply urea (46-0-0) at the rate of 50 kg/ha — split into two doses: half at 3 weeks after planting, half at 6 weeks. Place fertiliser in a band 5 cm from the plant and 3 cm deep — do NOT leave it on the soil surface. (2) Alternatively, apply well-composted poultry manure at 5 t/ha. (3) Intercrop with cowpea or groundnut — they fix atmospheric nitrogen into the soil for your maize. (4) Do NOT apply urea when the soil is dry; wait until after rainfall or irrigate lightly.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Eku oo, maize mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini mo le se?
answer: Chlorotic streaks following leaf veins indicate Maize Streak Virus transmitted by leafhoppers (Cicadulina spp.). There is no cure. (1) Remove and destroy all affected plants immediately. (2) Plant early at the onset of rains to avoid peak leafhopper populations. (3) Use streak-resistant hybrids: ZM 623, SC 627, or WH 505. (4) Do not plant maize near irrigated vegetable fields, which harbor leafhoppers year-round. (5) Apply carbofuran granules at 1.5 kg a.i./ha to the soil at planting to control early-season vectors. (6) Save seed only from completely disease-free plants.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo banana m anaghị eto nke ọma, akwukwo na-akpọnwụ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Upright, crowded leaves with a 'bunchy' appearance and dark green streaking on petioles indicate Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV) transmitted by the banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa). There is NO cure. (1) Uproot and destroy the entire plant including the corm — bury or burn it. (2) Control the aphid vector by spraying imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L on all surrounding plants. (3) Never use suckers from an affected field for new plantings. (4) Use tissue-culture plantlets — they are guaranteed virus-free. (5) Contact your agricultural extension office to report BBTV — it is a notifiable disease in most countries. (6) Quarantine any new planting material for 4 weeks.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo mango m anaghị eto nke ọma, akwukwo na-akpọnwụ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Small, immobile brown or white bumps on stems and leaf veins are scale insects. (1) Scrape off light infestations with a soft brush and soapy water. (2) Apply horticultural mineral oil at 2% (20 ml/L) ensuring thorough coverage — it smothers the scales. (3) Prune heavily infested branches and burn them. (4) Apply imidacloprid as a soil drench for persistent infestation (0.5 ml/L). (5) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds and parasitic wasps. Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill these beneficial insects. (6) Check nursery seedlings for scale BEFORE planting.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mo ni isoro pelu pepper mi, awon ewe re ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo sweet potato m anaghị eto nke ọma, akwukwo na-akpọnwụ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Distorted, mottled leaves and stunted growth on sweet potato indicate a viral infection, often transmitted by aphids or whiteflies. (1) Remove and destroy affected plants — viruses cannot be cured. (2) Control the insect vectors with neem oil (5 ml/L) or imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. (3) Use only certified virus-free planting material (vine cuttings or slips). (4) Remove weeds (especially morning glory and other Ipomoea species) that harbour the virus. (5) Plant a barrier crop (maize or sorghum) to disrupt insect movement into the field. (6) Wash hands and tools before handling healthy plants.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ina fama da matsalar maize ta. Ganyayyakin sun are showing signs of aflatoxin. Taya zan magance wannan?
answer: Mouldy or discoloured grains with a bitter taste are signs of aflatoxin contamination — a toxic fungus (Aspergillus flavus) that can cause liver damage in humans and animals. WARNING: Do NOT eat or sell mouldy grain. It is dangerous. Prevention for this season: (1) Dry harvested grain immediately to below 13% moisture. (2) Sort and remove all discoloured/mouldy grains by hand. (3) Store in clean, dry containers with good air circulation. (4) Use hermetic (sealed) storage bags if available — they cut off oxygen and stop fungal growth. For next season: plant resistant varieties, control insects that damage grain and create entry points for fungus, and harvest early at the right maturity.
source: ICRISAT dryland crops technical bulletin

question: Daalunu. groundnut m anaghị eto nke ọma, akwukwo na-akpọnwụ. Gini ka m ga-eme?
answer: Brown spots on groundnut leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Kedu. Ahụrụ m diamond-shaped gray lesions on leaves na osikapa m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: rice blast (Pyricularia oryzae) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungal spores carried by wind. Ngwọta: use resistant varieties like FARO 44. excess nitrogen makes blast worse.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for rice farmers

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo tea m nwere obere ahụhụ na akwụkwọ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate tea with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: A salaamun alaikum. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta pepper nursery e ndemri citta am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow pepper nursery e citta: start seeds in nursery. Ɗum wallitata sabo transplant after 6-8 weeks. space 45cm between plants, 60cm between rows.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for pepper farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. sunflower m nwere nsogbu — larvae in sunflower head feeding on seeds. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: head moth (Homoeosoma electellum) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. moth lays eggs on flowers. Ihe ị ga-eme: spray Bt at flowering. Echefula — plant resistant varieties.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for sunflower farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. Na ga dark streaks on leaves reducing photosynthesis a jikin ayaba ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: black sigatoka (Mycosphaerella fijiensis) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus spread by wind. Magani: spray fungicide regularly. remove infected leaves.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for plantain farmers

question: Ndewo. Ahụrụ m dark spots on leaves and vine dieback na ji m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: yam anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus spreads in rainy season. Ngwọta: use resistant variety TDr 95/19177. avoid planting in waterlogged soil.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for yam farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. kofi am woodi caɗeele — small holes in coffee berries with damage inside. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: coffee berry borer (Hypothenemus hampei) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. most serious coffee pest globally. Ko mbaɗata: harvest all ripe berries promptly. Woto yejjito — use broca traps with ethanol-methanol mix.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for coffee farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. Na ga brown spots on leaves a jikin alaiho ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: leaf spot (Alternaria amaranthi) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar fungus spread by rain. Magani: spray copper fungicide. reduce overhead irrigation.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for amaranth farmers

question: Eku agba mi, amaranth mi ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Small black or pale green insects clustered on stems and young growth are aphids. They suck sap and can transmit viruses. (1) Spray insecticidal soap (5 ml liquid soap in 1 L water) directly on the insects every 3 days. (2) Strong water spray can dislodge light infestations. (3) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (4) Encourage natural enemies: ladybirds (ladybugs), lacewings, and hoverflies — plant marigold or coriander near amaranth to attract them. (5) If infestation is severe and ants are present (ants farm aphids), apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. Remove ants with a sticky barrier around plant stems first.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. Na ga discolored grains with fungal growth a jikin dawa ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira grain mold. Yana yaduwa ta hanyar high humidity at grain filling. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately. Abin yi: harvest at physiological maturity. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit lori ata mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: bacterial spot (Xanthomonas campestris) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa bacteria spread by rain splash. Itoju: copper spray at transplanting. use disease-free seed from reliable source.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for pepper farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. barkono ta na da matsala — fruits rot from inside with maggots. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga pepper fruit fly. fly punctures fruit to lay eggs. Magani: harvest regularly before pest builds up. Kada ka manta — bag young fruits with paper.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for pepper farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le cashew planting fun oko kasu mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori cashew planting fun kasu: plant trees 10m apart. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe apply organic fertilizer. prune dead branches regularly.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for cashew farmers

question: Eku agba mi, okra mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Soft, foul-smelling roots indicate root rot caused by soil fungi (Pythium/Phytophthora). (1) Stop watering immediately — wet soil accelerates the rot. (2) Improve drainage by creating raised beds 30 cm high. (3) Remove and destroy all affected plants. (4) Drench the remaining soil with Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg of well-rotted compost. (5) For the next planting season, solarize the soil by covering beds with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks during the hottest months. (6) Rotate okra with maize or sorghum for at least 2 seasons before replanting.

question: Sannu da zuwa. ayaba ta na da matsala — larvae tunnel into corm causing toppling. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga banana weevil (Cosmopolites sordidus). adults hide in crop residues. Magani: use clean planting material (tissue culture). Kada ka manta — trap adults with pseudostem discs.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for plantain farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Ahụrụ m pods turn black with white flour-like coating na koko m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: black pod disease (Phytophthora megakarya) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na most serious cocoa disease in West Africa. Ngwọta: remove infected pods and spray copper fungicide. harvest ripe pods promptly — delay increases rot.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i orange powdery dust on undersides of leaves e kofi am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: coffee leaf rust (Hemileia vastatrix) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spread by wind. Nyawndam: spray copper fungicide. plant resistant varieties.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for coffee farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Ahụrụ m water-soaked spots on leaves na cotton m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for cotton farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo ri yellow leaves with white underside lori sunflower mi. Arun wo ni eyi?

source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for sunflower farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo ri yellow streaks on leaves lori agbado mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: maize streak virus (MSV) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa spread by leafhoppers. Itoju: remove infected plants early. no cure once plant is infected.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for maize farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. dankali am woodi caɗeele — holes in tubers with bitter taste. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: sweet potato weevil (Cylas puncticollis) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. weevil attacks underground. Ko mbaɗata: hill soil to cover exposed tubers. Woto yejjito — rotate crops for 2 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: No danyama. okra am woodi caɗeele — small round holes in leaves like shot pattern. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: Ɗo'o ko ñoɓɓere wi'eteende okra flea beetle. heavy infestation defoliates young plants. Safaare: neem oil spray and ash dusting. Woto yejjite — plant early to escape peak beetle season.
source: NASC-Adamawa, pest management advisory for okra farmers

question: Barka da rana. kabeji ta na da matsala — larvae create windows on leaves eating tissue. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga diamondback moth. most destructive brassica pest. Magani: spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis). Kada ka manta — use insect netting in nursery stage.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. shayi ta na da matsala — dark spots on leaves and young shoots. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: tea mosquito bug (Helopeltis antonii) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. bug pierces leaves and sucks sap. Abin da za ka yi: spray neem oil. Kada ka manta — prune affected branches.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for tea farmers

question: Wake na yana da kura (powder) fari a kan ganye. Magani?
answer: Kura fari a kan ganye na wake ita ce powdery mildew. (1) Cire ganyen da suka kamu da cutar — kona su. (2) Yayyafa soda (baking soda 5g/lita). (3) Yi amfani da mai na neem (neem oil 5ml/lita). (4) Juya amfanin gona. (5) Bada tazara tsakanin shuke-shuke. (6) Tuntuɓi jami'in noma (ADP) don shawara.

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Ahụrụ m sores in mouth and on hooves na mmiri ara m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: foot and mouth disease (FMD) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na highly contagious viral disease. Ngwọta: isolate infected animals. call veterinarian immediately.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for dairy farmers

question: Eku agba mi, groundnut mi ko dagba daradara, ewe re ti rerun. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: Aflatoxin contamination is caused by Aspergillus fungi and is a serious food safety risk — it can cause liver disease. Prevention is everything: (1) Harvest at the right maturity — do NOT delay harvest, especially if rains are expected. (2) Dry produce rapidly and thoroughly to below 13% moisture. Use raised drying racks, not bare ground. (3) Store in hermetic (airtight) bags — PICS bags or metal silos — away from heat and moisture. (4) Sort and discard any grains that are discoloured, shriveled, or moldy BEFORE storage. (5) Apply Aflasafe (biocontrol product available in Nigeria, Kenya) at 10 kg/ha 2-3 weeks before flowering. (6) NEVER feed mouldy grain to livestock.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ndewo. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi onion planting n'ugbo yorobo m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?

question: Bawo ni o. Mo ri wipe owu mi ni larvae bore into bolls causing them to drop. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?

question: Sannu da aiki. Na ga brown streaks inside tubers a jikin rogo ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?

question: E ku ise o. Mo ri wipe tii mi ni shoot tips wilt and die back. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?

source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for tea farmers

question: Nebbe am na nawa e nder suudu. Ko mbada?
answer: Nebbe de nawa e nder cuudi ko weevils. (1) Yooru nebbe den e naange haa selli. (2) Wintoo nder container di henndu naatataa. (3) Wintoo nder frigidaire (freezer) balde 7. (4) Nebbe ruftude den lartu. (5) Lartu cuudi di dadanotonoo. (6) Yeewtu e ADP.
source: ADP Bean Weevil Control; CIAT Storage Advisory

question: Mawɗe am na nawa kadi colli na ñaama ɗe. Ko mbaɗa?
answer: Colli ko torra mawnde e dow mawɗe. (1) Togo (scare) colli ɗi haa nguurtu — huutoro suturaaji (flags) maa karambu (tin cans). (2) Lartu gawri nder ngesa — woto wallito colli. (3) Demoo gabbe ɗe mbaɗi celluɗe: 'Seredo' — colli mbaawataa ñaamde. (4) Mbaɗ mawɗe saɗtina — woto accu e ngesa juuti. (5) Lartu bikkon maa gollooɓe ngam fogaade colli. (6) Yeewtu e ADP.
source: ADP Sorghum Bird Control; ICRISAT Bird Management

question: No wa'i. kossam am woodi caɗeele — cattle weak with weight loss. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: liver fluke (Fasciola gigantica) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. parasites from wet grazing areas. Ko mbaɗata: avoid grazing in swampy areas. Woto yejjito — give dewormer every 3 months.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for dairy farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta oil palm care e ndemri tamaro am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?

question: Daalunu. watermelon m na-acha odo odo na ntụpọ ojii. Gini ka m ga-eme?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo cocoa m na-acha odo odo na ntụpọ ojii. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Holes in pods with frass (insect droppings) indicate pod borer (Maruca vitrata / Helicoverpa armigera). (1) Hand-pick visible caterpillars at dawn. (2) Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2 g/L in the evening — it degrades in sunlight. (3) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L, soak 12 hrs, strain) weekly. (4) Plant early-maturing varieties to escape peak pest pressure. (5) Install pheromone traps (1 per 0.1 ha) to monitor moth flights. (6) After harvest, deep-plough (20-25 cm) to expose pupae to sunlight and birds. Pre-harvest interval for Bt: 0 days (safe up to harvest day).
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. biriiji am woodi caɗeele — holes in pods and root damage. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: termites woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. termites attack during dry periods. Ko mbaɗata: apply ash around plants. Woto yejjito — remove woody debris from field.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for groundnut farmers

question: Sannu da zuwa. auduga ta na da matsala — larvae bore into bolls causing them to drop. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo oil palm m anaghị eto nke ọma, akwukwo na-akpọnwụ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Yellowing patterns on oil palm indicate nutrient deficiency. (1) For nitrogen deficiency (uniform yellowing of older leaves): apply urea at 1-2 kg per tree per year, split into 2 applications. (2) For potassium deficiency (orange spotting on older leaves): apply muriate of potash at 2-3 kg per tree per year. (3) For magnesium deficiency (yellowing between veins of older leaves): apply kieserite at 0.5-1 kg per tree. (4) Apply empty fruit bunch (EFB) mulch at 60 t/ha around palms — it slowly releases nutrients. (5) Conduct a leaf analysis (take leaf #17 from 20 palms) to confirm which nutrients are deficient before large-scale fertiliser application.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu da aiki. Na ga purple-brown lesions on leaves that girdle them a jikin albasa ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?

answer: maize streak virus (MSV) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar spread by leafhoppers. Magani: remove infected plants early. no cure once plant is infected.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for maize farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta irrigation e ndemri tumate am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow irrigation e tumate: water at base of plant, avoid wetting leaves. Ɗum wallitata sabo reduce watering when fruits start ripening. drip irrigation gives best results.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for tomato farmers

question: Ndewo. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi cotton planting n'ugbo cotton m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka cotton planting na cotton: plant at start of rainy season. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na space 90cm between rows, 30cm between plants. prune dead branches to reduce disease.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for cotton farmers

question: Barka dai. Na ga pods turn black with white flour-like coating a jikin koko ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: black pod disease (Phytophthora megakarya) ce ke cutar amfanin gonar ka. Tana yaduwa ta hanyar most serious cocoa disease in West Africa. Magani: remove infected pods and spray copper fungicide. harvest ripe pods promptly — delay increases rot.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, disease diagnosis advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Ahụrụ m yellow and white streaked leaves na millet m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: downy mildew (Sclerospora graminicola) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus spread by wind and rain. Ngwọta: use resistant varieties. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for millet farmers

question: Kedu. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi cocoa cultivation n'ugbo koko m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka cocoa cultivation na koko: plant shade trees like plantain. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na maintain field cleanliness regularly. spray copper fungicide for black pod prevention.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo ri dark greasy spots on leaves and fruit rot lori tomatii mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: late blight (Phytophthora infestans) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus thrives in cool wet weather. Itoju: spray mancozeb preventively. rotate tomatoes away from potato fields.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for tomato farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi cabbage planting n'ugbo kabeji m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka cabbage planting na kabeji: start seeds in nursery. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na transplant after 4-5 weeks. space 45cm between plants.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri wipe ifunni mi ni ticks on cattle body sucking blood. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: ticks (Rhipicephalus microplus) lo n damu oko re. ticks transmit diseases like East Coast fever. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: dip or spray cattle with acaricide every 2 weeks. Ma gbagbe — maintain clean grazing areas to reduce ticks.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for dairy farmers

question: Sannu. onion na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: Purple-brown oval lesions on leaves and flower stalks indicate purple blotch (Alternaria porri). (1) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR iprodione at 1.5 g/L every 10 days. (2) Avoid excessive nitrogen — apply NPK 10-10-20 rather than high-nitrogen fertilisers. (3) Ensure good field drainage. (4) Rotate with non-allium crops for 3 years. (5) Harvest bulbs only when necks are fully dry; cure properly before storage. Pre-harvest interval: mancozeb 7 days.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Daalunu. millet m anaghị eto nke ọma, akwukwo na-akpọnwụ. Gini ka m ga-eme?
answer: Holes in stems and 'dead hearts' (withered central shoot) indicate stem borers (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus). (1) Pull out and destroy dead heart plants — larvae inside can spread to healthy plants. (2) Apply crushed neem leaves (1 kg/10 L water, steep 24 hours) into the leaf whorl — repeat weekly. (3) Apply carbofuran 3G granules at 0.75 kg a.i./ha into the whorl at knee-height stage. (4) After harvest, cut stubble to ground level and bury or burn crop residues to kill overwintering larvae. (5) Rotate with legumes (cowpea, groundnut) to break the pest cycle.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: E karo. Mo fe mo bi mo se le grazing rotation fun oko ifunni mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori grazing rotation fun ifunni: rotate grazing areas every week. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe allow pasture to rest between grazing. this prevents overgrazing and reduces disease.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for dairy farmers

question: Jam na. biriiji am woodi caɗeele — holes in pods and root damage. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: termites woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. termites attack during dry periods. Ko mbaɗata: apply ash around plants. Woto yejjito — remove woody debris from field.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for groundnut farmers

question: Eku oo, mo ri pe awon ewe cassava mi ti n ti n di ofeefee, won si ni awon eebi funfun kekere nisale ewe. Kini ohun ti mo le se lati ko won lo?
answer: This is cassava whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Do NOT spray broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill beneficial insects and make the problem worse. Immediate steps: (1) Remove and burn the worst-affected leaves. (2) Plant sunn hemp or marigold as a border crop — whiteflies avoid them. (3) If more than half the plants are infested, apply neem oil at 5ml per litre of water, spraying ONLY under the leaves, once every 7 days for 3 weeks. (4) Introduce natural predators like ladybird beetles if available in your area.
source: ICRISAT dryland crops technical bulletin

question: Ina fama da matsalar sweet potato ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna da kananan kwari akan ganye. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: Distorted, mottled leaves and stunted growth on sweet potato indicate a viral infection, often transmitted by aphids or whiteflies. (1) Remove and destroy affected plants — viruses cannot be cured. (2) Control the insect vectors with neem oil (5 ml/L) or imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L. (3) Use only certified virus-free planting material (vine cuttings or slips). (4) Remove weeds (especially morning glory and other Ipomoea species) that harbour the virus. (5) Plant a barrier crop (maize or sorghum) to disrupt insect movement into the field. (6) Wash hands and tools before handling healthy plants.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. Mi yi'i yellow leaves with white underside e sunflower am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: downy mildew woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus survives in soil. Nyawndam: use resistant varieties. rotate crops for 3 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for sunflower farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le pepper nursery fun oko ata mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori pepper nursery fun ata: start seeds in nursery. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe transplant after 6-8 weeks. space 45cm between plants, 60cm between rows.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for pepper farmers

question: Barka dai. Ina so in san yadda zan millet planting a aikin gero don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da millet planting a aikin gero: broadcast or plant in rows. Wannan yana taimakawa domin millet is highly drought-tolerant. plant at start of rains for good yield.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for millet farmers

question: Ina kwana. kanju ta na da matsala — grub bores into trunk causing branch dieback. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga cashew stem borer. entry holes with frass visible. Magani: inject neem oil into bore holes. Kada ka manta — keep trees healthy with organic mulch.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for cashew farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta harvesting and storage e ndemri nyebbe am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow harvesting and storage e nyebbe: harvest when pods are dry. Ɗum wallitata sabo store in airtight PICS bags. protect from bruchid weevils in storage.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for cowpea farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. mbayeeri am woodi caɗeele — deadheart in young seedlings. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: sorghum shoot fly (Atherigona soccata) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. flies lay eggs on young leaves. Ko mbaɗata: plant early to escape peak fly season. Woto yejjito — use resistant variety SAMSORG 40.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Ezigbo ohi. Ahụrụ m discolored grains with fungal growth na sorghum m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ọrịa a na-akpọ grain mold. Ọ na-agbasa site na high humidity at grain filling. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately. Ihe ị ga-eme: harvest at physiological maturity. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi mango tree care n'ugbo mangolo m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka mango tree care na mangolo: prune dead branches annually. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na apply organic fertilizer around base. irrigate during dry season.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for mango farmers

question: E pele o. Mo ri wipe jero mi ni chaffy grains with caterpillar inside panicle. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni millet head miner. moth pest of pearl millet. Ogba: use resistant variety ZATIP. Mase gbagbe pe — early planting avoids peak infestation.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for millet farmers

question: Jam na. oil palm am woodi caɗeele — larvae tunnel into trunk weakening the tree. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: Ɗo'o ko ñoɓɓere wi'eteende palm weevil (Rhynchophorus phoenicis). adults attracted to wounds on trunk. Safaare: avoid wounding trunk during pruning. Woto yejjite — pheromone traps for monitoring.
source: NASC-Adamawa, pest management advisory for oil palm farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i sores in mouth and on hooves e kossam am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: foot and mouth disease (FMD) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e highly contagious viral disease. Nyawndam: isolate infected animals. call veterinarian immediately.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for dairy farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri wipe anamo mi ni holes in tubers with bitter taste. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: sweet potato weevil (Cylas puncticollis) lo n damu oko re. weevil attacks underground. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: hill soil to cover exposed tubers. Ma gbagbe — rotate crops for 2 years.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo ri dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit lori ata mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: bacterial spot (Xanthomonas campestris) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa bacteria spread by rain splash. Itoju: copper spray at transplanting. use disease-free seed from reliable source.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for pepper farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. mangoro am woodi caɗeele — small puncture marks on fruit with larvae inside. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: mango fruit fly (Bactrocera dorsalis) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. female fly lays eggs under skin. Ko mbaɗata: use pheromone traps (methyl eugenol). Woto yejjito — collect fallen fruits and bury deep.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for mango farmers

question: No wa'i. marori am woodi caɗeele — central shoot drying out — deadheart symptom. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: rice stem borer woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. moth larvae bore into stem. Ko mbaɗata: apply carbofuran granules at panicle initiation. Woto yejjito — fields near wild grasses have higher infestation.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for rice farmers

question: Sannu. amaranth na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Mo ni isoro pelu tea mi, awon ewe re ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Reddish-brown discolouration of leaves with fine webbing indicates red spider mite (Oligonychus coffeae on tea). (1) Spray propargite at 1 ml/L OR fenazaquin at 1 ml/L ensuring thorough coverage of the underside of leaves. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L every 7 days. (3) Maintain shade — mites thrive in dry, hot, open conditions. (4) Rogue out heavily infested bushes. (5) Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides (especially synthetic pyrethroids) that kill predatory mites. Pre-plucking interval: 7 days.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Nnọọ. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi amaranth planting n'ugbo green m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka amaranth planting na green: broadcast seeds on prepared bed. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na water regularly. harvest after 4-6 weeks.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for amaranth farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo ri wipe ifunni mi ni ticks on cattle body sucking blood. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: ticks (Rhipicephalus microplus) lo n damu oko re. ticks transmit diseases like East Coast fever. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: dip or spray cattle with acaricide every 2 weeks. Ma gbagbe — maintain clean grazing areas to reduce ticks.

question: No wa'i. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta cashew planting e ndemri kasu am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow cashew planting e kasu: plant trees 10m apart. Ɗum wallitata sabo apply organic fertilizer. prune dead branches regularly.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for cashew farmers

question: Bawo ni. Mo ri wipe kofi mi ni small holes in coffee berries with damage inside. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: coffee berry borer (Hypothenemus hampei) lo n damu oko re. most serious coffee pest globally. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: harvest all ripe berries promptly. Ma gbagbe — use broca traps with ethanol-methanol mix.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for coffee farmers

question: Sannu da zuwa. gyada ta na da matsala — stunted plants with curled yellow leaves. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga groundnut aphid. aphids vector rosette virus. Magani: early planting avoids peak aphid season. Kada ka manta — neem seed extract spray.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for groundnut farmers

question: Ina kwana. koko ta na da matsala — feeding lesions on pods and shoots. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: cocoa mirids (Sahlbergella singularis) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. mirids inject toxic saliva. Abin da za ka yi: spray bifenthrin at recommended rates. Kada ka manta — shade management reduces mirid population.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Daalu nu. akpu m nwere nsogbu — yellow speckling on leaves. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Nke a bụ ahụhụ a na-akpọ cassava green mite (Mononychellus tanajoa). mites spread in dry season. Ngwọta: neem oil spray or acaricide. Echefula — severe infestation reduces root yield by 60%.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, pest management advisory for cassava farmers

question: Nnọọ. oka m nwere nsogbu — central leaves drying out (deadheart). Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: stem borer (Busseola fusca) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. moth lays eggs on underside of leaf. Ihe ị ga-eme: apply carbofuran at knee-height stage. Echefula — larva destroys stem from inside.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for maize farmers

question: Ndewo. kashu m nwere nsogbu — dead branches and holes in bark. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: cashew stem girdler na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. beetle girdles branches. Ihe ị ga-eme: prune affected branches. Echefula — maintain field cleanliness.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for cashew farmers

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Ahụrụ m blisters on leaves turning white na tii m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: blister blight (Exobasidium vexans) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus spreads in misty weather. Ngwọta: spray copper fungicide. prune for good air circulation.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for tea farmers

question: E ku ise o. Mo ri wipe ata mi ni fruits rot from inside with maggots. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni pepper fruit fly. fly punctures fruit to lay eggs. Ogba: harvest regularly before pest builds up. Mase gbagbe pe — bag young fruits with paper.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for pepper farmers

question: Sannu. oil palm na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: Brown spots on oil palm leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu. Mi yi'i yellow leaves and rotting trunk base e tamaro am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi banana planting n'ugbo unere m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?

question: Barka da rana. kanju ta na da matsala — grub bores into trunk causing branch dieback. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?

question: Ek'abo. Mo ri dark spots on leaves and vine dieback lori isu mi. Arun wo ni eyi?

question: Se dada ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le sunflower planting fun oko sunflower mi. Kini imoran re?

question: No wa'i. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta amaranth planting e ndemri kohi am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?

question: Sannu. Na ga brown spots on leaves a jikin alaiho ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?

question: Daalunu. Akwukwo cassava m nwere akara mosaic, osisi anaghị eto nke ọma. Gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Ọrịa ị na-ahụ bụ Cassava Mosaic Virus (CMD) — ọrịa kachasị njọ nke na-awakpo akpu. Ọ bụ whitefly na-ebute ya. O dighi ogwu ogwu — mgbochi ka mma. Ihe ị ga-eme: (1) Wepu osisi ndị na-arịa ọrịa ma kpochapu ha ozugbo — ejila ha mee kompositi. (2) Tinye osisi ohuru di iche iche na-eguzogide CMD dị ka TME 419 ma ọ bụ TMS 98/0581. (3) Gbaa mbọ hụ na ị na-achịkwa whiteflies — lee usoro whitefly na agri-001. (4) Ejila okpukpu ma ọ bụ mkpu site na osisi ndị na-arịa ọrịa. (5) Gbanwee ala — akụla akpu n'otu ala ahụ ruo oge abụọ. Nye akpu gị nri ọma site na itinye compost ma ọ bụ potaịsh ka osisi wee guzogide ọrịa. Maka enyemaka ọzọ, gakwuru ọrụ ugbo gị.
source: NRCRI Umudike Cassava Disease Guide; IITA Cassava Virology Lab

question: Sannu. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta millet planting e ndemri gawri am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow millet planting e gawri: broadcast or plant in rows. Ɗum wallitata sabo millet is highly drought-tolerant. plant at start of rains for good yield.

question: Barka da rana. Na ga leaves become narrow and bunched at top a jikin ayaba ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira banana bunchy top virus. Yana yaduwa ta hanyar aphid-transmitted, no cure. use virus-free suckers from certified source. Abin yi: uproot and destroy infected plants. use virus-free suckers from certified source.

question: Kedu. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi mango tree care n'ugbo mangolo m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?

question: A salaamun alaikum. dankali am woodi caɗeele — holes in tubers with bitter taste. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?
answer: sweet potato weevil (Cylas puncticollis) woni ko bonnata ndemri maa. weevil attacks underground. Ko mbaɗata: hill soil to cover exposed tubers. Woto yejjito — rotate crops for 2 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Bawo ni o. Mo ri wipe epa mi ni stunted plants with curled yellow leaves. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?

question: Kedu. Ahụrụ m orange powdery dust on undersides of leaves na kofi m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Ahụrụ m gray spots on lower leaves na oka m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: gray leaf spot (Cercospora zeae-maydis) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungal spores survive in crop residue. Ngwọta: spray mancozeb every 2 weeks. worsens in hot humid weather.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for maize farmers

question: Sannu. gyada ta na da matsala — stunted plants with curled yellow leaves. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?

question: Nnọọ. Ahụrụ m plants become stunted with clustered leaves na akidi m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

question: Mbaaɗa. koko am woodi caɗeele — feeding lesions on pods and shoots. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?

question: Sannu da zuwa. cocoa na ya are showing signs of black pod. Me zan yi don gba to?

question: Bawo ni. Mo ri wipe alubosa mi ni silvery streaks and twisted leaves. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?

question: Mo ni isoro pelu mango mi, awon ewe re ni awon kokoro funfun lori ewe. Jowo ran mi lowo.
answer: Dark bore holes on fruit and larvae inside the seed indicate mango seed weevil (Sternochetus mangiferae). The adult lays eggs on developing fruit and larvae tunnel into the seed. (1) Collect and destroy ALL fallen fruit and seeds — the weevil completes its lifecycle in the seed. (2) Spray lambda-cyhalothrin at 1 ml/L when fruit are marble-sized (2-3 cm). Repeat after 21 days. (3) Maintain orchard hygiene: remove and burn fallen leaves and debris. (4) Band tree trunks with sticky bands to trap weevils climbing up. (5) Harvest fruit slightly early (mature green stage) and store away from orchards.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: A salaamun alaikum. kasu am woodi caɗeele — dead branches and holes in bark. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?

question: Bawo ni. Mo ri yellow stunted leaves lori anamo mi. Arun wo ni eyi?

question: Bawo ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le weeding schedule fun oko pakí mi. Kini imoran re?

source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for cassava farmers

question: Sannu. okra na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: White powdery coating on leaves indicates powdery mildew (Erysiphales). It reduces photosynthesis and weakens plants. (1) Spray sulfur-based fungicide (micronized sulfur at 3 g/L) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) every 7 days. (2) Improve air circulation by wider spacing and removing excess foliage. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation — water at the base of plants. (4) Spray a solution of 1 part milk to 9 parts water — milk proteins have antifungal properties effective against powdery mildew. Apply weekly. (5) Remove and burn heavily infected leaves. Pre-harvest interval for sulfur: 1 day.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Jam na. Mi yi'i leaves become narrow and bunched at top e banana am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: Ɗo'o ko rafi wi'eteedo banana bunchy top virus. O saakotoo e laawol aphid-transmitted, no cure. use virus-free suckers from certified source. Ko potɗaa waɗde: uproot and destroy infected plants. use virus-free suckers from certified source.

question: Jam na. Mi yi'i discolored grains with fungal growth e mbayeeri am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. tii m nwere nsogbu — dark spots on leaves and young shoots. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?

question: A salaamun alaikum. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta groundnut planting e ndemri biriiji am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?

source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for groundnut farmers

question: Barka da rana. Na ga dark spots on leaves and vine dieback a jikin doya ta. Wace cuta ce wannan?

question: Sannu. Mi yi'i yellow streaks on leaves e masar am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?

question: A salaamun alaikum. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta grazing rotation e ndemri kossam am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?

question: Kedu. akidi m nwere nsogbu — holes in pods and root damage. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?

question: Sannu. amaranth am woodi caɗeele — caterpillar webs leaves together and feeds inside. Ɗume ñoɓɓere woni ndee, ɗume mbaɗata?

source: NASC-Adamawa, pest management advisory for amaranth farmers

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo cassava m nwere obere ahụhụ na akwụkwọ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Brown leaf spots on cassava are caused by Cercospora fungi. (1) Remove severely infected lower leaves and burn them. (2) Spray mancozeb (2 g/L of water) or copper oxychloride (3 g/L) every 10-14 days during wet weather. (3) Improve air circulation by widening plant spacing to 1 m × 1 m. (4) Apply mulch to prevent rain splash that spreads spores. (5) For the next crop, choose a well-drained field and apply 2 t/ha of well-rotted compost to strengthen plant resistance. Fungicide pre-harvest interval: minimum 21 days.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Barka dai. wake ta na da matsala — stunted plants with yellow leaves. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: bean fly (Ophiomyia phaseoli) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. fly larvae bore into stems. Abin da za ka yi: plant early to escape peak fly season. Kada ka manta — apply mulch around plants.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for beans farmers

question: Barka dai. Ina so in san yadda zan yam planting a aikin doya don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?

question: Sannu. cassava na ba ya girma sosai, ganye suna bushewa. Me zan yi?
answer: The yellow-green leaf pattern you describe is Cassava Mosaic Disease caused by geminiviruses transmitted by whiteflies. There is no chemical cure. (1) Uproot and burn ALL affected plants immediately — do NOT use them as planting material. (2) Use certified mosaic-resistant varieties: TME 419, TMS 30572, or IITA-TMS-I011412. (3) Plant stakes at the recommended spacing of 1 m × 1 m. (4) Avoid recycling stakes from infected fields. (5) Intercrop with maize or cowpea to reduce whitefly populations. Contact your nearest IITA or NRCRI extension office for free resistant planting material.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Daalunu. pepper m nwere obere ahụhụ na akwụkwọ. Gini ka m ga-eme?
answer: Brown spots on pepper leaves indicate leaf spot disease (Cercospora / Alternaria spp.). (1) Remove and destroy affected leaves. (2) Spray mancozeb at 2.5 g/L OR copper oxychloride at 3 g/L every 10-14 days. (3) Improve air circulation through wider spacing. (4) Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet. (5) Apply well-rotted compost at 2 t/ha to boost plant immunity. (6) Rotate with non-host crops for 2 seasons.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Ahụrụ m blisters on leaves turning white na tii m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for tea farmers

question: Ndewo. mangolo m nwere nsogbu — small puncture marks on fruit with larvae inside. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?

source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for mango farmers

question: Ndewo. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi tea planting n'ugbo tii m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?

question: Sannu. cotton na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Angular, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown indicate bacterial blight (Xanthomonas spp.). (1) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L + streptomycin at 0.3 g/L at first sign. (2) Avoid working in the field when plants are wet — bacteria spread through water. (3) Use only acid-delinted, certified seed. (4) Rotate with maize or sorghum for 2-3 years. (5) Remove and burn all crop residues after harvest. (6) Avoid excessive nitrogen which promotes lush, susceptible growth.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ndewo. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi sorghum planting n'ugbo sorghum m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?

question: Sannu. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta pepper nursery e ndemri citta am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo sorghum m anaghị eto nke ọma, akwukwo na-akpọnwụ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: Small pink-purple flowering weeds attached to the roots of your sorghum are Striga (witchweed). Each plant produces 50,000+ seeds that persist in soil for 15+ years. (1) Hand-pull ALL Striga plants BEFORE they flower — pull and burn them. (2) Do NOT plant sorghum in the same field next season — rotate with groundnut or cowpea which trigger Striga seed germination but are not parasitised ('suicidal germination'). (3) Apply imazapyr-resistant maize varieties (StrigAway / IR-maize) coated with herbicide at planting. (4) Apply 2 t/ha of well-composted farmyard manure — it improves soil fertility and reduces Striga emergence. (5) Deep-plough after harvest to bury seeds below the germination zone.
source: FAO Agricultural Guidelines, 2024; reviewed agricultural literature

question: E pele o. Mo ri wipe kòkó mi ni feeding lesions on pods and shoots. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni cocoa mirids (Sahlbergella singularis). mirids inject toxic saliva. Ogba: spray bifenthrin at recommended rates. Mase gbagbe pe — shade management reduces mirid population.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. kuɓewa ta na da matsala — small round holes in leaves like shot pattern. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: okra flea beetle (Podagrica uniforma) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. heavy infestation defoliates young plants. Abin da za ka yi: neem oil spray and ash dusting. Kada ka manta — plant early to escape peak beetle season.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for okra farmers

question: Ndewo. Ahụrụ m white powdery coating on leaves na okwuru m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: powdery mildew na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus spreads in dry season. Ngwọta: spray sulfur fungicide. remove infected leaves.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for okra farmers

question: Ututu oma. Ahụrụ m dark greasy spots on leaves and fruit rot na tomato m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ọrịa a na-akpọ late blight (Phytophthora infestans). Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus thrives in cool wet weather. rotate tomatoes away from potato fields. Ihe ị ga-eme: spray mancozeb preventively. rotate tomatoes away from potato fields.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for tomato farmers

question: Ek'abo. Mo ri wipe baba mi ni deadheart in young seedlings. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: sorghum shoot fly (Atherigona soccata) lo n damu oko re. flies lay eggs on young leaves. Ohun ti o ye ki o se: plant early to escape peak fly season. Ma gbagbe — use resistant variety SAMSORG 40.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, pest management advisory for sorghum farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri angular brown spots on leaves lori ere mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: angular leaf spot lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spread by rain splash. Itoju: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for beans farmers

question: Ek'abo. Mo ri leaves become narrow and bunched at top lori ogede mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: banana bunchy top virus lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa aphid-transmitted, no cure. Itoju: uproot and destroy infected plants. use virus-free suckers from certified source.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for banana farmers

question: Sannu. rogo ta na da matsala — yellow speckling on leaves. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga cassava green mite (Mononychellus tanajoa). mites spread in dry season. Magani: neem oil spray or acaricide. Kada ka manta — severe infestation reduces root yield by 60%.

question: Nnọọ. mangolo m nwere nsogbu — small puncture marks on fruit with larvae inside. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: mango fruit fly (Bactrocera dorsalis) na-akpata nsogbu n'ubi gị. female fly lays eggs under skin. Ihe ị ga-eme: use pheromone traps (methyl eugenol). Echefula — collect fallen fruits and bury deep.
source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for mango farmers

question: E pele o. Mo ri wipe agbado mi ni shallow holes in whorl leaves with caterpillar frass. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda). armyworm moth lays eggs at night on young maize — larvae feed inside whorl. Ogba: azadirachtin neem spray at early instar stage. Mase gbagbe pe — infestation spreads fast without control — act within 3 days of first damage.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for maize farmers

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi cabbage planting n'ugbo kabeji m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka cabbage planting na kabeji: start seeds in nursery. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na transplant after 4-5 weeks. space 45cm between plants.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Kedu. Ahụrụ m water-soaked spots on leaves na cotton m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: bacterial blight (Xanthomonas campestris pv. malvacearum) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na bacteria spread by rain. Ngwọta: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for cotton farmers

question: Shanuna (dairy cow) tana kafin ƙirji (udder) kumbura. Magani?
answer: Kumburin ƙirji (udder) na saniya yana nufin mastitis. (1) KIRA likitan dabbobi (vet) nan da nan. (2) Wanke ƙirjin saniya kafin kiɗa (milking). (3) Yi amfani da 'teat dip' bayan kiɗa (kowace rana). (4) Yi amfani da tawul (towel) daban ga kowace saniya. (5) Kiɗa saniya lafiya da farko, sannan saniya mai mastitis. (6) Tsaftace wurin kiɗa kowace rana. (7) Idan saniya tana da zazzaɓi (fever), tana buƙatar antibiotics — likitan dabbobi zai ba da magani.
source: NAERLS Mastitis Control; DVS Veterinary Guide

question: Ututu oma. ogidi m nwere nsogbu — larvae tunnel into corm causing toppling. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?

source: NRCRI-Umudike, pest management advisory for plantain farmers

question: E karo. Mo ri wipe jero mi ni chaffy grains with caterpillar inside panicle. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?

question: Nnọọ. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi water management n'ugbo osikapa m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka water management na osikapa: maintain 2-5cm water depth during tillering. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na drain field 10 days before harvest. alternate wetting and drying saves water without yield loss.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for rice farmers
