question: Sannu. yam na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Dark, sunken lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit indicate anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). (1) Remove and destroy all infected plant parts — do NOT compost them. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: A salaamun alaikum. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta okra planting e ndemri la'ano am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow okra planting e la'ano: sow seeds 2-3cm deep. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 60cm between rows, 30cm between plants. okra needs full sun and well-drained soil.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for okra farmers

(2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L or mancozeb at 2.5 g/L every 10-14 days, starting at flowering. (3) Prune to improve air circulation and reduce humidity. (4) Apply 2-3 cm of organic mulch to prevent rain splash. (5) For the next season, use certified disease-free seed and practice 3-year crop rotation with cereals. Pre-harvest interval: 7-14 days depending on the product.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ụtụtụ ọma. Ahụrụ m discolored grains with fungal growth na sorghum m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

question: Ndewo. Ahụrụ m water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown na agwa m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

question: Sannu. sorghum na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grey-purple fuzz underneath indicate downy mildew (Peronospora spp.). (1) Spray metalaxyl-M + mancozeb at 2 g/L OR phosphorous acid at 3 ml/L every 7-10 days. (2) Improve field drainage and air circulation. (3) Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening — water early morning instead. (4) Remove crop debris after harvest. (5) Use disease-free seed for the next planting. (6) For onion, cure bulbs properly (7-10 days in sun) before storage.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Daalunu. Osisi tomato m are showing signs of tomato leaf miner. Gini ka m gba mee?

question: Daalu nu. Ahụrụ m purple-brown lesions on leaves that girdle them na yorobo m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?

question: E ku ise. Mo fe mo bi mo se le harvesting and storage fun oko ere mi. Kini imoran re?

question: Ezigbo ụbọchị. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi oil palm care n'ugbo nkwu m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?

question: Eku agba mi, cassava mi ti n di ofeefee pelu awon abawon dudu. Kini o ye ki n se nitori ki n le gba ikore?
answer: This is cassava whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Do NOT spray broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill natural enemies like Encarsia wasps and make outbreaks worse. Instead: (1) Spray insecticidal soap or 0.5% neem oil solution every 7 days for 3 weeks. (2) Remove and burn heavily infested leaves. (3) Plant maize or sorghum as barrier crops between cassava rows to disrupt whitefly movement. (4) Use yellow sticky traps (1 per 10 m²). If infestation persists, apply imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L as a LAST resort, observing a 14-day pre-harvest interval. Wash hands and produce after application.
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Sannu da aiki. Ina so in san yadda zan grazing rotation a aikin kiwo don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?

source: NRCRI Umudike, pest management advisory for yam farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. dankali ta na da matsala — larvae tunnel into tubers making them bitter. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga sweet potato weevil (Cylas formicarius). adults feed on leaves and stems. Magani: use weevil-free planting material. Kada ka manta — hilling up soil around base prevents entry.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for sweet potato farmers

question: Barka da rana. ayaba ta na da matsala — larvae tunnel into corm causing toppling. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga banana weevil (Cosmopolites sordidus). adults hide in crop residues. Magani: use clean planting material (tissue culture). Kada ka manta — trap adults with pseudostem discs.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for plantain farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri dark spots on fruit and leaves lori gbogiri mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: anthracnose lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spread by rain splash. Itoju: spray fungicide at flowering. rotate crops.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for watermelon farmers

question: Sannu. cocoa na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Holes in pods with frass (insect droppings) indicate pod borer (Maruca vitrata / Helicoverpa armigera). (1) Hand-pick visible caterpillars at dawn. (2) Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2 g/L in the evening — it degrades in sunlight. (3) Apply neem seed kernel extract (50 g/L, soak 12 hrs, strain) weekly. (4) Plant early-maturing varieties to escape peak pest pressure. (5) Install pheromone traps (1 per 0.1 ha) to monitor moth flights. (6) After harvest, deep-plough (20-25 cm) to expose pupae to sunlight and birds. Pre-harvest interval for Bt: 0 days (safe up to harvest day).
source: NRCRI Extension Bulletin; reviewed agricultural literature

question: E ku ise. Mo ri white fuzzy growth on leaves lori alubosa mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: onion downy mildew lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus spreads in humid conditions. Itoju: reduce overhead irrigation. plant resistant varieties.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for onion farmers

question: Ndewo. Achọrọ m ịmata otu m ga-esi cashew planting n'ugbo kashu m. Gịnị ka ị ga-adụ m ọdụ?
answer: Nke a bụ ndụmọdụ m maka cashew planting na kashu: plant trees 10m apart. Nke a na-enyere aka n'ihi na apply organic fertilizer. prune dead branches regularly.
source: NRCRI Umudike, cultural practice advisory for cashew farmers

question: Ina fama da matsalar maize ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Yaya zan magance wannan?
answer: The small holes and shredded young leaves indicate fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda). Act immediately — one larva can destroy 3 whorls. (1) Hand-pick and crush egg masses (fuzzy white patches) and visible larvae, especially at dawn or dusk. (2) Apply a 5% neem seed extract (50 g ground neem seed per litre of water, soak 12 hrs, strain) into the whorl of each plant — the larvae ingest it and stop feeding within hours. (3) In maize, add dry sand or ash (1 pinch per whorl) — it desiccates the larvae. (4) As a last resort, apply emamectin benzoate at 0.4 ml/L or spinosad at 0.3 ml/L. (5) Push-pull: plant Desmodium between rows to repel moths and Napier grass around fields to trap them. Pre-harvest interval for spinosad: 3 days.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: No wa'i. Mi yi'i orange powdery dust on undersides of leaves e kofi am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: coffee leaf rust (Hemileia vastatrix) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spread by wind. Nyawndam: spray copper fungicide. plant resistant varieties.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for coffee farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta plantain planting e ndemri ayaba am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow plantain planting e ayaba: use healthy suckers from reliable source. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 3m between plants. apply mulch to conserve moisture.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for plantain farmers

question: Daalu o. mangolo m nwere nsogbu — small puncture marks on fruit with larvae inside. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Nke a bụ ahụhụ a na-akpọ mango fruit fly. female fly lays eggs under skin. Ngwọta: use pheromone traps (methyl eugenol). Echefula — collect fallen fruits and bury deep.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, pest management advisory for mango farmers

question: Sannu. cabbage na suna yin rawaya tare da bakaken tabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Small holes in leaves and green caterpillars that wriggle violently when disturbed indicate diamondback moth (Plutella xylostella). (1) Spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki) at 2 g/L every 7 days — it targets caterpillars only. (2) Apply neem oil at 5 ml/L. (3) Use pheromone traps to monitor moth populations. (4) Rotate insecticide groups — diamondback moth rapidly develops resistance. Alternate Bt with spinosad at 0.3 ml/L. (5) Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest. (6) Plant trap crop: Indian mustard attracts moths away from cabbage.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Daalu nu. koko m nwere nsogbu — feeding lesions on pods and shoots. Kedu ụdị ahụhụ nke a bụ, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Nke a bụ ahụhụ a na-akpọ cocoa mirids (Sahlbergella singularis). mirids inject toxic saliva. Ngwọta: spray bifenthrin at recommended rates. Echefula — shade management reduces mirid population.
source: NRCRI-Umudike, pest management advisory for cocoa farmers

question: Sannu. kabeji ta na da matsala — small holes in leaves and green larvae. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: diamondback moth (Plutella xylostella) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. moth lays eggs on leaf undersides. Abin da za ka yi: spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis). Kada ka manta — rotate crops to break life cycle.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. alaiho ta na da matsala — holes in stems and wilting leaves. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: amaranth stem borer ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. moth larvae bore into stems. Abin da za ka yi: spray neem oil. Kada ka manta — remove infected plants.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for amaranth farmers

question: No wa'i. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta onion planting e ndemri albasare am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow onion planting e albasare: direct seed or use nursery transplants. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 20cm between rows, 10cm between plants. onions need full sun exposure.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for onion farmers

question: Ina fama da matsalar yam ta. Ganyayyakin sun suna da alamar mosaic a kan ganye, kuma tsiron baya girma sosai. Taya zan magance wannan?
answer: Wannan matsala ce da ke damun yam. Ina ba da shawarar ka tuntuɓi ma'aikatar aikin gona ta gari domin ganin takamaiman maganinta. Kada ka jira — kamuwa da cuta na iya yaɗuwa cikin sauri. Allah ya sa mu dace.
source: NAERLS-Extension, general advisory for yam farmers

question: Se dada ni. Mo ri yellow leaves and rotting trunk base lori ope mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: basal stem rot (Ganoderma boninense) lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa fungus survives in soil and wood debris. Itoju: remove and burn infected trees. keep field clear of wood debris.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for oil palm farmers

question: Sannu da aiki. Ina so in san yadda zan mango tree care a aikin mangwaro don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da mango tree care a aikin mangwaro: prune dead branches annually. Wannan yana taimakawa domin apply organic fertilizer around base. irrigate during dry season.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for mango farmers

question: Nnọọ. Ahụrụ m dark spots on ripening fruit na mangolo m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na fungus spreads via rain splash. Ngwọta: spray fungicide before harvest. hot water dip after harvest.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for mango farmers

question: Eku agba mi, mo ri awon leaf mi ti won n yellow, mo si ri awon small white fly ni abe leaf. Kini mo le se?
answer: Ohun ti o n se apejuwe ni eepi funfun ti gbin (Bemisia tabaci). Eepi funfun n mu 'cassava mosaic virus' wa, ati pe o le fa pipadanu ikore ti o to 70%. Ohun ti o le se: (1) Mu awon ewe ti o ni arun kuro ki o si sun won — ma ko won sinu kompositi. (2) Fun ogba kekere, lo epo neem (5 milimita fun lita omi kan) ti o fi fo labe ewe, ni gbogbo ose meje fun ose meta. (3) Gbin 'sunn hemp' tabi marigold ni eti oko — eepi funfun ko feran awon ohun ogbin wonyi. (4) Ni akoko ti nbo, gbin eya cassava ti o ni idaduro si 'cassava mosaic virus' bii TME 419 tabi TMS 98/0581. Ranti pe oogun ti o lagbara pupo le pa awon kokoro ti o n ran wa lowo, nitori naa ma lo neem tabi ose Dudu nikan. Ti o ba nilo iranlowo siwaju, lo si ile ise agbeko agbegbe re.
source: IITA Cassava Pest Management Guide, 2023; reviewed by Dr. A. Okeowo, agronomist

question: Bawo ni. Mo fe mo bi mo se le groundnut planting fun oko epa mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori groundnut planting fun epa: sow seeds 5cm deep. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe space 60cm between rows, 15cm between plants. groundnut needs well-drained sandy loam soil.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for groundnut farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo fe mo bi mo se le pepper nursery fun oko ata mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori pepper nursery fun ata: start seeds in nursery. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe transplant after 6-8 weeks. space 45cm between plants, 60cm between rows.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for pepper farmers

question: Sannu. tumatir ta na da matsala — mines inside leaves creating translucent patches. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: Wannan matsala ce daga tomato leaf miner (Tuta absoluta). moth pest spreads rapidly. Magani: use pheromone traps and neem spray. Kada ka manta — can destroy whole field in 2 weeks without control.
source: NAERLS-Zaria, pest management advisory for tomato farmers

question: No wa'i. Mi yi'i angular brown spots on leaves e nyebbe am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: angular leaf spot woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spread by rain splash. Nyawndam: use disease-free seed. rotate crops for 2 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for beans farmers

question: Barka dai. Ina so in san yadda zan tomato nursery a aikin tumatir don in samu riba mai kyau. Me za ku ce?
answer: Ga shawarata game da tomato nursery a aikin tumatir: start seeds in nursery bed. Wannan yana taimakawa domin transplant after 3-4 weeks. space 60cm between plants, 90cm between rows.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, cultural practice advisory for tomato farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. Mi yi'i dark spots on leaves and vine dieback e dundu am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: yam anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads in rainy season. Nyawndam: use resistant variety TDr 95/19177. avoid planting in waterlogged soil.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for yam farmers

question: No wa'i. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta plantain planting e ndemri ayaba am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow plantain planting e ayaba: use healthy suckers from reliable source. Ɗum wallitata sabo space 3m between plants. apply mulch to conserve moisture.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for plantain farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. Mi yi'i blisters on leaves turning white e shayi am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: blister blight (Exobasidium vexans) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus spreads in misty weather. Nyawndam: spray copper fungicide. prune for good air circulation.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for tea farmers

question: Sannu. Miɗo yiɗi anndude no mi waɗirta amaranth planting e ndemri kohi am. Ɗume wasiyiiji maa?
answer: Wasiyanke am dow amaranth planting e kohi: broadcast seeds on prepared bed. Ɗum wallitata sabo water regularly. harvest after 4-6 weeks.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, cultural practice advisory for amaranth farmers

question: A salaamun alaikum. Mi yi'i yellow leaves with white underside e sunflower am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: downy mildew woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus survives in soil. Nyawndam: use resistant varieties. rotate crops for 3 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for sunflower farmers

question: Assalamu alaikum. barkono ta na da matsala — fruits rot from inside with maggots. Wane irin kwaro ne wannan kuma me zan yi?
answer: pepper fruit fly (Bactrocera latifrons) ne ke damun amfanin gonar ka. fly punctures fruit to lay eggs. Abin da za ka yi: harvest regularly before pest builds up. Kada ka manta — bag young fruits with paper.
source: NAERLS/ABU Zaria, pest management advisory for pepper farmers

question: Kedu. Ahụrụ m water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown na agwa m. Kedu ọrịa nke a bụ?
answer: cowpea bacterial blight na-emebi ihe ọkụkụ gị. Ọ na-agbasa site na rain splash spreads bacteria. Ngwọta: apply copper-based fungicide. use certified disease-free seed.
source: NRCRI Umudike, disease diagnosis advisory for cowpea farmers

question: Nnukwu m, akwukwo cabbage m nwere obere ahụhụ na akwụkwọ. Biko nyere m aka.
answer: V-shaped yellow lesions at leaf margins with blackened veins indicate black rot (Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris). (1) Remove and destroy affected plants — the bacteria spread through water. (2) Spray copper oxychloride at 3 g/L to protect remaining plants. (3) Use hot-water treated seed (50°C for 25 minutes) for the next planting. (4) Never work in the field when plants are wet. (5) Rotate with non-crucifer crops (maize, cowpea) for 3-4 years. (6) Control weeds in the cabbage family (wild mustard, shepherd's purse) that harbour the bacteria.
source: IITA Crop Management Guide; reviewed agricultural literature

question: Ek'abo. Mo fe mo bi mo se le plantain planting fun oko ogede mi. Kini imoran re?
answer: Eyi ni imoran mi lori plantain planting fun ogede: use healthy suckers from reliable source. Eyi yoo se iranlowo nitori pe space 3m between plants. apply mulch to conserve moisture.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, cultural practice advisory for plantain farmers

question: E ku aaro. Mo ri wipe kabeji mi ni larvae create windows on leaves eating tissue. Iru kokoro wo ni eyi ati kini mo le se?
answer: Eyi je kokoro ti a n pe ni diamondback moth. most destructive brassica pest. Ogba: spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis). Mase gbagbe pe — use insect netting in nursery stage.
source: IAR&T-Ibadan, pest management advisory for cabbage farmers

question: Mbaaɗa. Mi yi'i purple-brown lesions on leaves that girdle them e albasare am. Ɗume rafi woni ɗo'o?
answer: onion purple blotch (Alternaria porri) woni rafi bonnata ndemri maa. Ɗum saakitoo e fungus Alternaria porri. Nyawndam: spray mancozeb every 10 days. rotate away from allium fields for 3 years.
source: ILRI/IAR Samaru, disease diagnosis advisory for onion farmers

question: E ku ise. Mo ri discolored grains with fungal growth lori baba mi. Arun wo ni eyi?
answer: grain mold lo n ba oko re je. O n tan kaakiri nipa high humidity at grain filling stage. Itoju: harvest at physiological maturity. dry grains to 12% moisture immediately.
source: IAR&T Obafemi Awolowo University, disease diagnosis advisory for sorghum farmers
